BURSEVI:v10p325#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p325#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p325#2/r1.claim: The false dawn resembles a wolf’s tail and carries no legal ruling; the true dawn triggers fasting and prayer. Its emergence spreads light and sends people and animals out for provision, resembling resurrection.
BURSEVI:v10p325#2/r1.anchor: فجران مستطيل كذنب السرحان وهو الكاذب ولا يتعلق به حكم ومستطير وهو الصادق الذي يتعلق به الصوم والصلاة

BURSEVI:v10p325#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p325#2/r2.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v10p325#2/r2.claim: Kashifi interprets dawn as the time when beloveds commune with God.
BURSEVI:v10p325#2/r2.anchor: سوكند بصبح كه وقت مناجات دوستانست

BURSEVI:v10p325#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p325#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p325#2/r3.claim: Other interpretations identify dawn as the morning of Arafah, when pilgrims go to the plain and perform supplications, citing the report “Hajj is Arafah.”
BURSEVI:v10p325#2/r3.anchor: أو أقسم بصباح عرفة لأنه يوم شرف يتوجه فيه الحجاج إلى جبل عرفات

BURSEVI:v10p325#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p325#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p325#2/r4.claim: Dawn may instead mean the Day of Sacrifice, a great day for the required circumambulation, shaving, and stoning; it is reported as the greater Hajj day.
BURSEVI:v10p325#2/r4.anchor: أو صباح يوم النحر لأنه يوم عظيم أيضا ويقع فيه الطواف المفروض والحلق والرمي ويروى أن يوم النحر يوم الحج الأكبر

BURSEVI:v10p325#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p325#2/r5.speaker: التبيان
BURSEVI:v10p325#2/r5.claim: Tabyan offers further dawn images: the New Year, Friday as the poor person’s pilgrimage, miraculous water from the Prophet’s fingers or Moses’ stone, Salih’s she-camel from rock, springs, rain, or sinners’ tears.
BURSEVI:v10p325#2/r5.anchor: انفجار آب از أصابع حضرت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BURSEVI:v10p325#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p325#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p325#2/r6.claim: The dawn imagery also urges repentance: if you carry a stain, wash it away with streams of tears.
BURSEVI:v10p325#2/r6.anchor: بران ازدوسر شمه ديده جوى ورآلايشى داري ازخود بشوى

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r1.claim: The preceding surah's signs establish God's power, wisdom, and providence, which entail a Day of accountability and reward; otherwise His mercy and wisdom would be contradicted.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r1.anchor: when He possesses great power and wisdom

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r2.claim: The Prophet's role is to warn through the signs in heaven and earth, even when people cannot see them; he cannot guide the blind.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r2.anchor: His only responsibility is to warn them through these signs even if they are not able to see them. He cannot guide the blind.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p299/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p299/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p299/r1.claim: The oaths establish that God alone governs the world, brings things forth and removes them, grants respite, and acts within no rival's authority.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p299/r1.anchor: In His hands are the reins of everything. It is He Who brings forth everything and it is He Who makes them disappear.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p299/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p299/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p299/r2.claim: Fajr is the moment night darkness disappears and daylight appears at the horizon; unlike fajr, subh spans dawn and the time after sunrise, so it is qualified in oaths.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p299/r2.anchor: but also the time after sunrise.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p299/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p299/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p299/r3.claim: The dawn oath resembles oaths in al-Muddaththir: night recedes and morning appears as evidence that the Day of Judgment is a great event.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p299/r3.anchor: the night bears witness when it turns its back and the morning when it appears

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p300/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p300/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p300/r1.claim: Dawn's daily transformation symbolizes the appointed arrival of Judgment: after death people will rise as if from sleep, just as night gives way to morning; a waking supplication alludes to this.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p300/r1.anchor: The time of fajr brings the message of a great change

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p300/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p300/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p300/r3.claim: Oaths should be read as evidence for the surah's claim, not assumed to concern sacred objects; identify the claim and compare parallel Qur'anic passages.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p303/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p303/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p303/r5.claim: The first and last oaths are primary and contrast dawn with departing night; the middle oaths are secondary signs between them supporting the opening claim.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p303/r5.anchor: Further deliberation on the first four verses shows that the oaths

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p304/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p304/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p304/r1.claim: Contrasting forces of nature coexist in harmony; only one wise, powerful sovereign can reconcile them, since competing deities would destroy the world.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p304/r1.anchor: these conflicting elements have great harmony and accord between them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p304/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p304/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p304/r2.claim: Pairs reach completion with their counterparts; likewise this world is incomplete without an afterlife, where God will judge the conflict of good and evil and reward or punish people.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p304/r2.anchor: there should come a day of justice in which the Lord of the worlds, with full authority, control and knowledge hold people accountable and then reward His good people and punish those who had spread disorder

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p305/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p305/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p305/r1.claim: Without a Day of Judgment, good and evil would be treated alike and creation would be purposeless; 68:35–36 makes the same objection to denying accountability.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p305/r1.anchor: are We to treat alike the obedient and the criminals?

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p305/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p305/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p305/r2.claim: Daylight and night sustain material life, while ease and hardship train the moral and spiritual self in gratitude and patience, preparing people for the state described in 89:28.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p305/r2.anchor: they will be happy with their Lord

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p305/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p305/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p305/r3.claim: The alternation of night and day shows that every created thing is governed by God, so even powerful people cannot escape His control.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p305/r3.anchor: It is He who releases and restrains it and it is He who sets it free.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p305/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p305/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p305/r4.claim: The oath's signs of release and restraint emphasize God's control, as illustrated by the possibility of perpetual night or day in 28:71–72.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p305/r4.anchor: no one, however much powerful he may be, should arrogantly reckon that he is beyond His control.

QUSHAYRI:v3p419/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p419/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p419/r1.claim: The basmala unsettles the poor and disorients the enamored, but brings mercy to lovers; worshippers may satisfy it by reciting, while lovers must offer their lives.
QUSHAYRI:v3p419/r1.anchor: كلمة قهارة للقلوب ، ولكن لا لكل قلب ، كلمة لا سبيل لهها لكل عقل

QUSHAYRI:v3p419/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p419/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p419/r2.claim: Fajr is the first burst of morning light, described as both elongated and short; interpretations identify the dawn of Muharram, Dhu al-Hijjah, water emerging from rocks, or the saints' opening worship.
QUSHAYRI:v3p419/r2.anchor: الفجر انفجار الصبح وهو اثنان : مستطيل وقصير

SULAMI:v2p394/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p394/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p394/r1.claim: Dawn is Muhammad, through whom the lights of faith dawn and the darkness of unbelief disappears.
SULAMI:v2p394/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء رحمه الله : ﴿ والفجر ﴾ هو محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

TUSTARI:89:1/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:89:1/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:89:1/r1.claim: The outward meaning of dawn is the morning.

TUSTARI:89:4/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:89:4/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:89:4/r2.claim: Inwardly, the dawn is Muhammad, from whom the lights of faith, obedience, and both worlds burst forth.
TUSTARI:89:4/r2.anchor: منه تفجرت أنوار الإيمان وأنوار الطاعات وأنوار الكونين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p468/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p468/r5.speaker: أبو الدينار الأعرابي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p468/r5.claim: Abu al-Dinar al-Aʿrabi adds tanwin to al-fajr, al-watr, and yasr; Ibn Khalawayh compares the usage with Arabs' pausal tanwin at rhyme endings, even on verbs or definite forms.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p468/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو الدينار الأعرابي: والفجر، والوتر، ويسر بالتنوين في الثلاثة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p469/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p469/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p469/r1.claim: A poem illustrates tanwin-like endings in open rhymes; grammarians discuss this in unrestricted rhymes and in ordinary pausal speech.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p469/r1.anchor: وهذا ذكره النحويون في القوافي المطلقة إذا لم يترنم الشاعر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p469/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p469/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p469/r5.claim: Al-Fajr most naturally means dawn in general, not one specified day; other reports identify it with the Day of Sacrifice, Friday, Dhul-Hijjah, the night at Jamʿ, or the first day of Muharram.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p469/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p469/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p469/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas also explains al-fajr as the whole day, the dawn prayer and its recitation, or the dawn of springs in rock.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p469/r6.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أيضا: الفجر: النهار كله

FARRA:v3p259#2/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p259#2/r1.speaker: الأسود بن يزيد
FARRA:v3p259#2/r1.claim: Al-Aswad ibn Yazīd says al-fajr is the familiar dawn and the ten nights are the first ten of Dhū al-Ḥijja.
FARRA:v3p259#2/r1.anchor: عن أبى إسحق عن الأسود بن يزيد في قوله: «والفجر» قال: هو فجركم هذا. «وليال عشر» قال: عشر الأضحى.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p119/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p119/r1.speaker: علي وابن عباس وابن الزبير
ALUSI-FULL:v30p119/r1.claim: The dawn is the familiar dawn, as transmitted from Ali, Ibn Abbas, Ibn al-Zubayr, and others; Alusi considers the true dawn especially fitting for the oath because it governs fasting and prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p119/r1.anchor: كما روي عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه وابن عباس وابن الزبير

ALUSI-FULL:v30p119/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p119/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p119/r2.claim: Dawn is named for splitting the night broadly; false dawn does not determine fasting or prayer, whereas true dawn does, and the likely referent is the true dawn in general.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p119/r2.anchor: وأصله شق الشيء شقا واسعاوسمى الصبح

ALUSI-FULL:v30p119/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p119/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v30p119/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid identify the oath as the dawn of the Sacrifice day.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p119/r3.anchor: وعن ابن عباس ومجاهد فجر يوم النحر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p119/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p119/r4.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p119/r4.claim: Ikrima identifies it as Friday's dawn.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p119/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p119/r5.speaker: الضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v30p119/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies it as the dawn of Dhu al-Hijja.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p119/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p119/r6.speaker: مقاتل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p119/r6.claim: Muqatil identifies it as the dawn of the night at Muzdalifa.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p119/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p119/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p119/r7.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas identifies it as Muharram's dawn, the dawn of the year; a similar view is related from Qatada.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p119/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه قال هو فجر المحرم فجر السنة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p119/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p119/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p119/r8.claim: Other reports from Ibn Abbas take the dawn to mean the whole daytime, or the dawn prayer; the prayer interpretation is also related from Zayd ibn Aslam.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p119/r8.anchor: وعن الحبر أيضا أنه النهار كله وأخرج ابن جرير عنه أيضا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p412#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p412#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p412#2/r1.claim: Abu Salih reports Ibn Abbas’s view that dawn is the breaking of morning each day; Ikrima agrees.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p412#2/r1.anchor: روى أبو صالح عن ابن عباس قال: هو انفجار الصبح كل يوم وهو قول عكرمة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p412#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p412#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p412#2/r2.claim: Atiyya reports Ibn Abbas’s alternative that the oath refers to the dawn prayer.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p412#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p412#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p412#2/r3.claim: Qatada identifies it as the first dawn of Muharram, from which the year begins.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p412#2/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة: هو فجر أول يوم من المحرم، تنفجر منه السنة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p412#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p412#2/r4.speaker: الضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p412#2/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says it is the dawn of Dhu al-Hijja, linked with the following ten nights.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p412#2/r4.anchor: وقال الضحاك: فجر ذي الحجة لأنه [قرنت] (2) به الليالي العشر.

BAYDAWI-FULL:89:1-3/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:1-3/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:1-3/r1.claim: الفجر is dawn or its breaking, as in 81:18, or the dawn prayer.
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:1-3/r1.anchor: { والفجر } أقسم بالصبح أو فلقه كقوله:

BINTSHATI:v2p125/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p125/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p125/r1.claim: The surah is early Meccan, tenth in revelation order, revealed after al-Layl and before al-Duha.
BINTSHATI:v2p125/r1.anchor: السورة مكية مبكرة، ترتيبها العاشرة في النزول. نزلت بعد سورة الليل وقبل سورة الضحى.

BINTSHATI:v2p125/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p125/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p125/r2.claim: Fajr is the first morning light as it appears in night's darkness, and by extension the time when that light appears.
BINTSHATI:v2p125/r2.anchor: والفجر ضوء الصباح أول ظهوره في سواد الليل، ومنه يطلق على وقت ظهور هذا الضوء.

BINTSHATI:v2p125/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p125/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p125/r3.claim: The sensory root image is water bursting from earth; Arabic uses related forms for gushing and eruptions such as volcanoes.
BINTSHATI:v2p125/r3.anchor: ولعل الاستعمال الحسي الأول للمادة، في تفجر الماء من الأرض.

BINTSHATI:v2p125/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p125/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p125/r4.claim: Metaphorically, emergence in light, goodness, generosity, and virtue is fajr, while emergence in evil is fujur and in sin is fujur or fisq; al-Ayyam al-Fijar were four pre-Islamic battle days.
BINTSHATI:v2p125/r4.anchor: فهو فجر، وفي الفسق والمعصية فجور

BINTSHATI:v2p125/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p125/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p125/r5.claim: The root occurs 24 times in the Quran, including ten verbs mostly about water gushing; the sole non-water verbal use is the threat that a person would transgress.
BINTSHATI:v2p125/r5.anchor: جاءت المادة في أربعة وعشرين موضعاً، منها عشر مرات أفعالاً، يغلب مجئ الفعل منها في تفجر الماء وتفجيره،

BINTSHATI:v2p126/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p126/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p126/r1.claim: Fajr is rare as a Quranic noun for water: it names rivers in 17:91 and a spring in 76:6; the root also names wickedness opposite piety.
BINTSHATI:v2p126/r1.anchor: وتفجير عين بآية (الإنسان 6) ووردت ست مرات في الفجور: مقابلاً بالتقوى في آية (الشمس 8)

BINTSHATI:v2p126/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p126/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p126/r2.claim: The dawn sense appears in six verses; 2:187 identifies its sign as the white thread becoming distinct from the dark, and 17:78 places it after nightfall's darkness.
BINTSHATI:v2p126/r2.anchor: وتدل آية البقرة على أن علامة مطلع الفجر، أن يتبين الخيط الأبيض من الخيط الأسود، إيذاناً بإنبثاق النور في الظلمة،

BINTSHATI:v2p126/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p126/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p126/r3.claim: Ghasaq is darkness mixed with first light at the end of night, or lingering light after sunset.
BINTSHATI:v2p126/r3.anchor: والغسق ظلام مختلط ببوادر النور في آخر الليل. أو بقايا الضوء بعد مغيب النهار وغروب الشمس.

BINTSHATI:v2p126/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p126/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI:v2p126/r4.claim: Al-Tabari reports Ibn Abbas's view that fajr means the entire day; the author rejects it in favor of the familiar dawn at the night's end.
BINTSHATI:v2p126/r4.anchor: وإنما هو الفجر المعهود عند تبين الخيط الأبيض من سواد الليل

BINTSHATI:v2p126/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p126/r5.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI:v2p126/r5.claim: Al-Raghib derives dawn from splitting, like earth split by springs, and calls it the one that splits the night; the author prefers the broader sense of emergence.
BINTSHATI:v2p126/r5.anchor: وقد رده "الراغب" إلى معنى الشق "كما في تفجير الأرض عيوناً وأنهاراً

BINTSHATI:v2p126/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p126/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p126/r6.claim: The author derives fajr from emergence or outburst, whether a deliberate physical opening, spontaneous eruption, or figurative moral emergence.
BINTSHATI:v2p126/r6.anchor: ونؤثر أن نرده كذلك إلى دلالة الإنبثاق والإنبعاث، يكون حسياً بشق متعمد، كما يكون تلقائياً كالإنفجار

BINTSHATI:v2p126/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p126/r7.speaker: الطبري
BINTSHATI:v2p126/r7.claim: Al-Tabari, al-Naysaburi, and al-Zamakhshari supply an omitted genitive, either 'Lord of dawn' or 'Quran of dawn.'
BINTSHATI:v2p126/r7.anchor: قيل، ورب الفجر، أو وقرآن الفجر، على ما نقل الإمام الطبري

BINTSHATI:v2p126/r8.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p126/r8.speaker: الرازي
BINTSHATI:v2p126/r8.claim: Specific proposed dawns include the morning of sacrifice, the first dawn of Muharram, or springs from which water and life emerge.
BINTSHATI:v2p126/r8.anchor: قيل هو "فجر النحر لأنه يوم الضحايا والقرابين" أو هو "فجر المحرم لأنه أول يوم من كل سنة

BINTSHATI:v2p135/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p135/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p135/r1.claim: The author rejects readings that inflate every oath object into a symbol of honor and confuse exaltation with divine wisdom in creation.
BINTSHATI:v2p135/r1.anchor: دون أن نتجشم عناء التأويل بما يفخم كل مقسم به ويعظمه، أو نخلط بين التفخيم والتعظيم والتشريف

BINTSHATI:v2p135/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p135/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p135/r2.claim: The succession of dawn, crescent, and night makes sensory light and darkness an image of truth emerging after prolonged moral darkness and tyranny.
BINTSHATI:v2p135/r2.anchor: فالفجر إذ ينبثق نوره فينسخ ظلمة الليل، والهلال إذ يبزغ وليداً إثر المحاق ويمضى رويداً في دحر الظلام

BINTSHATI:v2p135/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p135/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p135/r3.claim: The natural contrasts prepare for testing through wealth or deprivation and the opposed outcomes of tyrants and the tranquil soul.
BINTSHATI:v2p135/r3.anchor: أو بالفقر والحرمان، وما يظن معهما من إكرام أو إهانة، ثم التقابل في المصير ما بين عذاب الطاغين المغرورين، ونعيم النفس المطمئنة.

BINTSHATI:v2p135/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p135/r4.speaker: الطبري
BINTSHATI:v2p135/r4.claim: Al-Tabari says the verses should not be burdened with claims unsupported by transmitted reports or reason; al-Razi and al-Zamakhshari also criticize the commentators' sprawling speculation.
BINTSHATI:v2p135/r4.anchor: ومن ثم لا نحمل هذه الآيات "ما لم تدل عليه بخبر ولا عقل" كما قال الإمام الطبري،

BINTSHATI:v2p136/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p136/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI:v2p136/r1.claim: The author says the surrounding passage is better read as a call to admonition and reflection.

BINTSHATI:v2p136/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p136/r2.speaker: الفخر الرازي
BINTSHATI:v2p136/r2.claim: Al-Razi identifies 'your Lord is surely watching' as the oath's answer and treats the intervening passage as parenthetical.
BINTSHATI:v2p136/r2.anchor: والفخر الرازي، يرى أن الجواب هو: {إن ربك لبالمرصاد} وما بينه وبين القسم معترض.

BINTSHATI:v2p136/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p136/r3.speaker: ابن القيم
BINTSHATI:v2p136/r3.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim takes the answer as implicit in the oath's inclusion of what was brought to Abraham and Muhammad.

BINTSHATI:v2p136/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p136/r4.speaker: أوب حيان
BINTSHATI:v2p136/r4.claim: Abu Hayyan and Muhammad Abdu say the omitted answer is the end of al-Ghashiya, because that surah precedes al-Fajr in the printed Quran.

BINTSHATI:v2p136/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p136/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p136/r5.claim: The author rejects an answer supplied by al-Ghashiya: it was revealed 58 surahs after al-Fajr, so adjacency in the printed order cannot leave this oath suspended until then.
BINTSHATI:v2p136/r5.anchor: ولكنها في ترتيب النزول متأخرة عنها، فالغاشية نزلت في أواخر العهد المكي،

BIQAI-FULL:v8p413#s089/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p413#s089/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p413#s089/r1.claim: Surat al-Fajr argues for return and reckoning, the ending of al-Ghashiya; dawn breaks after the prior day and sleepers rise from the lesser death of sleep to seek livelihood, then face reward or punishment.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p413#s089/r1.anchor: مقصودها الاستدلال على آخر الغاشية الإياب والحساب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p413#s089/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p413#s089/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p413#s089/r2.claim: The basmala portrays God as gathering people after their disintegration, granting explanation that prepares whom He wills for faith, and reserving contentment and gardens for His allies.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p413#s089/r2.anchor: جامع العباد بعد تمزيقهم بما له من العظمة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p413#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p413#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p413#2/r1.claim: The conclusion of al-Ghashiya announces return and reckoning; renewed night and day, and Hajj rites performed in pilgrim clothing with talbiya and travel to sacred places, recall resurrection.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p413#2/r1.anchor: لما ختمت تلك بأنه لا بد من الإياب والحساب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p413#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p413#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p413#2/r2.claim: The oath’s Fajr is the dawn of the Sacrifice day, when pilgrims enter the sanctuary, leave consecration, and receive God’s hospitality; a new day follows one that has passed without a change in essence.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p413#2/r2.anchor: وهو فجر يوم النحر الذي هو أول الأيام الآخذة في الإياب إلى بيت الله الحرام

NAHHAS:v5p217/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p217/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p217/r1.claim: The noun is genitive under the wāw of oath.

NAHHAS:v5p217/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p217/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v5p217/r2.claim: He gives three explanations of the dawn: the dawn of Muḥarram, daytime, or the dawn prayer.
NAHHAS:v5p217/r2.anchor: وعن ابن عباس في معناه ثلاثة أقوال منها أنه فجر السنة المحرم وأنه النهار وأنه صلاة الفجر

NAHHAS:v5p217/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p217/r3.speaker: مسروق
NAHHAS:v5p217/r3.claim: He identifies it with the dawn people see each day.
NAHHAS:v5p217/r3.anchor: وأما مسروق فقال هو فجركم هذا

NAHHAS:v5p217/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p217/r4.speaker: أهل الكوفة
NAHHAS:v5p217/r4.claim: The Kufan grammarians identify dawn's light as whiteness.

NAHHAS:v5p217/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p217/r5.speaker: أهل المدينة
NAHHAS:v5p217/r5.claim: The Medinan grammarians identify dawn's light as redness, supported by Arab usage for a garment dyed red.
NAHHAS:v5p217/r5.anchor: وأهل المدينة يقولون هو الحمرة وقد حكي عن العرب ثوب مشفق ومشفق أي مصبوغ بالحمرة

DURR-FULL:v8p497/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p497/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p497/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr say Surat al-Fajr was revealed in Mecca; the section also classifies the surah as Meccan and thirty verses.

DURR-FULL:v8p497/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p497/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p497/r2.claim: The Prophet rebuked Muadh for overlong prayer and directed him to recite shorter chapters, including the chapters beginning with glorification, the sun, dawn, and night.

DURR-FULL:v8p497/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p497/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبير
DURR-FULL:v8p497/r3.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says God swears by the dawn.
DURR-FULL:v8p497/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله بن الزبير في قوله

DURR-FULL:v8p497/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p497/r4.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
DURR-FULL:v8p497/r4.claim: Maymun ibn Mihran says God may swear by any of His creation, while no one may swear except by God.

DURR-FULL:v8p497/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p497/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p497/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the dawn as daybreak.

DURR-FULL:v8p497/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p497/r6.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p497/r6.claim: Ikrima identifies the dawn as morning, and elsewhere as dawn at Muzdalifa on the morning of the gathering.
DURR-FULL:v8p497/r6.anchor: عبد بن حميد عن عكرمة في قوله:

DURR-FULL:v8p497/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p497/r7.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p497/r7.claim: Mujahid says the dawn is specifically that of the Sacrifice Day, not every dawn; Muhammad ibn Ka'b agrees.
DURR-FULL:v8p497/r7.anchor: ابن أبي حاتم عن مجاهد في قوله

DURR-FULL:v8p497/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p497/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p497/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the dawn as the dawn prayer.
DURR-FULL:v8p497/r8.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن ابن عباس

DURR-FULL:v8p497/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p497/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p497/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the dawn as Muharram, the first dawn of the year.

DURR-FULL:v8p497/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p497/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p497/r10.claim: The Prophet says the best fasting after Ramadan is in God's month of Muharram, and the best prayer after the obligatory prayer is night prayer.
DURR-FULL:v8p497/r10.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: أفضل الصيام

DURR-FULL:v8p497/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p497/r11.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v8p497/r11.claim: Ali tells a man asking which month to fast after Ramadan to fast Muharram, God's month, which includes the day God accepted one people's repentance and forgave others.

DURR-FULL:v8p499/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p499/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p499/r1.claim: The Prophet said that, if he lived, he would order fasting one day before or after Ashura.
DURR-FULL:v8p499/r1.anchor: وأخرج البيهقي عن ابن عباس أن رسول الله

DURR-FULL:v8p499/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p499/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p499/r2.claim: He urged fasting the ninth and tenth of Muharram to differ from the Jews.
DURR-FULL:v8p499/r2.anchor: وأخرج البيهقي عن ابن عباس قال:

DURR-FULL:v8p499/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p499/r3.speaker: أبو جبلة
DURR-FULL:v8p499/r3.claim: While traveling with Ibn Shihab, he saw him fast Ashura; Ibn Shihab said Ramadan could be made up later, but Ashura would pass.
DURR-FULL:v8p499/r3.anchor: وأخرج البيهقي عن أبي جبلة قال:

DURR-FULL:v8p499/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p499/r4.speaker: أبو موسى
DURR-FULL:v8p499/r4.claim: Because Jews honored Ashura as a festival, the Prophet told Muslims to fast it.
DURR-FULL:v8p499/r4.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة عن أبي موسى

DURR-FULL:v8p499/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p499/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v8p499/r5.claim: The Prophet described Ashura as a day the prophets used to fast and told Muslims to fast it.
DURR-FULL:v8p499/r5.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة عن أبي هريرة

DURR-FULL:v8p499/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p499/r6.speaker: جابر
DURR-FULL:v8p499/r6.claim: The Prophet promised that whoever gives generously to family on Ashura will receive provision throughout the year.

DURR-FULL:v8p499/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p499/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p499/r7.claim: The Prophet promised yearlong provision to whoever expands provision for dependents on Ashura.
DURR-FULL:v8p499/r7.anchor: وأخرج البيهقي عن ابن مسعود قال:

DURR-FULL:v8p499/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p499/r8.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
DURR-FULL:v8p499/r8.claim: The Prophet promised that whoever gives generously to family on Ashura will receive provision for the rest of the year.
DURR-FULL:v8p499/r8.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي الدنيا والبيهقي عن أبي سعيد الخدري

DURR-FULL:v8p499/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p499/r9.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v8p499/r9.claim: The Prophet promised yearlong provision for generosity on Ashura; al-Bayhaqi said the individually weak chains gain strength together.
DURR-FULL:v8p499/r9.anchor: وأخرج البيهقي عن أبي هريرة قال:

DURR-FULL:v8p499/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p499/r10.speaker: إبراهيم بن محمد بن المنتشر
DURR-FULL:v8p499/r10.claim: A traditional saying held that generosity to one's family on Ashura brings abundant provision throughout the year.
DURR-FULL:v8p499/r10.anchor: وأخرج البيهقي عن إبراهيم بن محمد بن المنتشر

DURR-FULL:v8p499/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p499/r11.speaker: عروة عن ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p499/r11.claim: A report, which al-Bayhaqi weakened, says applying antimony to the eyes on Ashura prevents eye inflammation forever.
DURR-FULL:v8p499/r11.anchor: وأخرج البيهقي وضعفه عن عروة عن ابن عباس

DURR-FULL:v8p499/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p499/r12.speaker: جابر
DURR-FULL:v8p499/r12.claim: The Prophet interpreted the ten nights as the first ten of Dhu al-Hijjah, the odd as Arafah, and the even as the Day of Sacrifice.
DURR-FULL:v8p499/r12.anchor: أخرج أحمد والنسائي والبزار وابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن مردويه والحاكم وصححه والبيهقي في الشعب عن جابر

DURR-FULL:v8p503/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p503/r13.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p503/r13.claim: His recitation ran from the dawn oath through the night oath; he said these oaths affirm that the Lord is ever watchful.
DURR-FULL:v8p503/r13.anchor: أخرج ابن المنذر عن ابن مسعود أنه قرأ

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3423/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3423/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبير
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3423/r1.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says God swears by the dawn.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3423/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن الزبير في قوله : والفجر قال : قسم اقسم الله به

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3423/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3423/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3423/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the dawn as daybreak.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3423/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : والفجر قال : فجر النهار

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3423/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3423/r3.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3423/r3.claim: Ikrimah identifies the dawn as morning.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3423/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة في قوله : والفجر قال : هو الصبح

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3423/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3423/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3423/r4.claim: Mujahid restricts the oath to the dawn of the Day of Sacrifice, not every dawn.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3423/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله : والفجر قال : فجر يوم النحر وليس كل فجر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p476#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p476#3/r1.speaker: جمهور من المتأولين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p476#3/r1.claim: Most interpreters take the dawn as the familiar dawn that rises each day.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p476#3/r1.anchor: قال جمهور من المتأولين: الفجر هنا المشهور الطالع كل يوم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p476#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p476#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p476#3/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas also interprets dawn as the whole daytime.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p476#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p476#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وزيد بن أسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p476#3/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas and Zayd ibn Aslam identify the dawn with the morning prayer and its recitation, the Quran of dawn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p476#3/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا وزيد بن أسلم: «الفجر» الذي أقسم الله به، صلاة الصبح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p476#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p476#3/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p476#3/r4.claim: Mujahid says the oath refers to the dawn of the Sacrifice Day.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p476#3/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد: إنما أراد فجر يوم النحر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p476#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p476#3/r5.speaker: الضحاك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p476#3/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak says it means the dawn of Dhu al-Hijjah.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p476#3/r5.anchor: وقال الضحاك: المراد فجر ذي الحجة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p476#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p476#3/r6.speaker: مقاتل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p476#3/r6.claim: Muqatil identifies the dawn as that of the night at Muzdalifah.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p476#3/r6.anchor: وقال مقاتل: المراد فجر ليلة جمع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p476#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p476#3/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p476#3/r7.claim: Another view from Ibn Abbas is the first dawn of Muharram, the beginning of the year.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p476#3/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: أيضا: المراد فجر أول يوم من المحرم، لأنه فجر السنة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p476#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p476#3/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p476#3/r8.claim: An unnamed interpretation takes dawn as springs emerging from rocks and elsewhere.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p476#3/r8.anchor: وقيل المراد فجر العيون من الصخور وغيرها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p476#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p476#3/r9.speaker: عكرمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p476#3/r9.claim: Ikrima identifies it as the dawn of Friday.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p476#3/r9.anchor: وقال عكرمة: المراد فجر يوم الجمعة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p102/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p102/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، علي بن عبيد الله
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p102/r1.claim: Fajr is the opening of darkness into morning; the noun derives from splitting open, like water bursting through, and fājir describes one who breaks from obedience.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p102/r1.anchor: الفجر انفجار الظلمة عن الصبح وانفجر الماء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p102/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p102/r2.speaker: علي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p102/r2.claim: The oath refers to the familiar dawn, the beginning of daytime.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p102/r2.anchor: الفجر المعروف الذي هو بدء النهار قاله علي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p102/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p102/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، عكرمة، زيد بن أسلم، القرظي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p102/r3.claim: They likewise identify it as the morning breaking each day.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p102/r3.anchor: هو انفجار الصبح كل يوم وبهذا قال عكرمة وزيد بن أسلم والقرظي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p102/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p102/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p102/r4.claim: Another interpretation is the dawn prayer, transmitted by ʿAṭiyya.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p102/r4.anchor: صلاة الفجر رواه عطية عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p102/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p102/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p102/r5.claim: Another interpretation is the whole day, named for its beginning; Abū Naṣr transmits this from Ibn ʿAbbās.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p102/r5.anchor: النهار كله فعبر عنه بالفجر لأنه أوله وروى هذا المعنى أبو نصر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p102/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p102/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p102/r6.claim: The oath refers specifically to the dawn of the Day of Sacrifice.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p102/r6.anchor: فجر يوم النحر خاصة قاله مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p102/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p102/r7.speaker: الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p102/r7.claim: The oath refers to the dawn of the first day of Dhū al-Ḥijja.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p102/r7.anchor: فجر أول يوم من ذي الحجة قاله الضحاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p102/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p102/r8.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p102/r8.claim: The oath refers to the first day of Muḥarram, from which the year begins.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p102/r8.anchor: أول يوم من المحرم تنفجر منه السنة قاله قتادة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p390/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p390/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p390/r1.claim: After a man left Muadh's overly long prayer and Muadh called him a hypocrite, the Prophet warned Muadh against driving people away and recommended several short surahs, including al-Fajr.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p390/r1.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "أفتان يا معاذ؟ أين أنت من {سبح اسم ربك الأعلى} {والشمس وضحاها} {والفجر}

JISHUMI:v10p7395/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7395/r1.speaker: أبي بن كعب
JISHUMI:v10p7395/r1.claim: A report from the Prophet promises forgiveness to one who recites al-Fajr and a light on the Resurrection Day to one who recites it daily.
JISHUMI:v10p7395/r1.anchor: وعن أبي بن كعب، عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: من قرأ سورة (الفجر) غفر له

JISHUMI:v10p7395/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7395/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7395/r2.claim: After the previous chapter said that all creatures return to God and He judges them, this chapter emphasizes that He watches over them, warning and encouraging them.
JISHUMI:v10p7395/r2.anchor: ولما ختم السورة المتقدمة بأن مصير الخلق إليه وحسابهم عليه، افتتح هذه السورة بتأكيد ذلك بالقسم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p749/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p749/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p749/r1.claim: The oath is by dawn, as in other dawn descriptions, or by the dawn prayer.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p749/r1.anchor: أقسم بالفجر كما أقسم بالصبح في قوله : { والصبح إذا أسفر } ( المدثر : 34 )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p749/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p749/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p749/r8.claim: Another reading joins al-fajr and al-watr with tanwin, which substitutes for a final lengthening letter; Ibn Abbas reads ليال عشر with an annexation meaning nights of ten days.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p749/r8.anchor: وقرىء ( والفجر ) والوتر ، ويسر : بالتنوين ، وهو التنوين الذي يقع بدلا من حرف الإطلاق

SAMIN-DURR:89:1/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:1/r1.speaker: ابن الأنباري
SAMIN-DURR:89:1/r1.claim: Ibn al-Anbari identifies ‘inna rabbaka la-bil-mirsad’ as the stated answer to the oath by dawn.
SAMIN-DURR:89:1/r1.anchor: جواب هذا القسم قيل: مذكور وهو قوله إن ربك لبالمرصاد [الفجر: 14] قاله ابن الأنباري.

SAMIN-DURR:89:1/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:1/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:89:1/r2.claim: Alternatively, the oath’s answer is omitted but understood as a promise to requite each person, indicated by the enumeration of what happened to earlier peoples.
SAMIN-DURR:89:1/r2.anchor: وقيل: محذوف لدلالة المعنى عليه، أي: لنجازين أحد بما عمل

SAMIN-DURR:89:1/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:1/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:89:1/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari supplies ‘He will surely punish’, supported by the account of former peoples being struck down.
SAMIN-DURR:89:1/r3.anchor: وقدر الزمخشري: " ليعذبن " قال: " يدل عليه ألم تر

SAMIN-DURR:89:1/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:1/r4.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:89:1/r4.claim: The Shaykh infers the omitted answer from the preceding sura’s ending: people return to God, who holds them to account.
SAMIN-DURR:89:1/r4.anchor: وقدره الشيخ بما دلت عليه خاتمة السورة قبله، لإيابهم إلينا وحسابهم علينا

SAMIN-DURR:89:4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:89:4/r2.claim: An omitted noun may be supplied, making the oath by the dawn prayer or by the Lord of dawn.
SAMIN-DURR:89:4/r2.anchor: وقيل: ثم مضاف محذوف، أي: وصلاة الفجر أو ورب الفجر

SAMIN-DURR:89:4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:4/r3.speaker: أبو الدينار الأعرابي
SAMIN-DURR:89:4/r3.claim: Most readers do not nunate ‘al-fajr’, ‘al-watr’, and ‘yasr’; Abu al-Dinar al-A‘rabi nunates all three, treating verse endings like poetic rhymes.
SAMIN-DURR:89:4/r3.anchor: والعامة على عدم التنوين في " الفجر " و " الوتر " و " يسر ". وأبو الدينار الأعرابي بتنوين الثلاثة

SAMIN-DURR:89:4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:4/r4.speaker: ابن خالويه
SAMIN-DURR:89:4/r4.claim: Ibn Khalawayh calls the poetic nunation ‘tanwin al-tarannum’, including nunation at verse endings even for verbs and definite nouns; his quoted couplet illustrates it.
SAMIN-DURR:89:4/r4.anchor: قال ابن خالويه: " هذا ما روي عن بعض العرب أنه يقف على أواخر القوافي بالتنوين

SAMIN-DURR:89:4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:4/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:89:4/r5.claim: Some grammarians object to the label ‘tanwin al-tarannum’ and prefer ‘tanwin tark al-tarannum’; another type, ‘tanwin al-ghali’, appears on a closed rhyme and is disputed, with different rules from ordinary nunation.
SAMIN-DURR:89:4/r5.anchor: وقد عاب بعضهم قول النحويين " تنوين الترنم " وقال: بل ينبغي أن يسموه بتنوين ترك الترنم

SAMIN-DURR:89:4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:4/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:89:4/r6.claim: The reader has treated the Qur’anic endings like rhyme endings; the author cites similar forms in al-Ahzab and al-Ra‘d as parallels.
SAMIN-DURR:89:4/r6.anchor: والحاصل أن هذا القارىء أجرى الفواصل مجرى القوافي ففعل فيها ما يفعل فيها

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p264#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p264#2/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p264#2/r1.claim: Fajr is the sunrise-side burst of dawn from the eastern horizon; it has two forms. The first is a narrow vertical streak, called false dawn by some because it can mislead about the coming day, and it has no effect on prayer or fasting; the second spreads horizontally and is true dawn, on which prayer and fasting rules depend.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p264#2/r1.anchor: قسم أقسم الله تعالى به , وهو انفجار الصبح من أفق المشرق , وهما فجران : فالأول منهما مستطيل كذنب السرحان

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p264#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p264#2/r2.speaker: الشاعر
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p264#2/r2.claim: The cited verse uses المصدق for true dawn that gives a truthful sign of morning.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p265/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p265/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p265/r1.claim: The true dawn determines the rules of prayer and fasting.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p265/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p265/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p265/r2.claim: The oath by dawn may mean the day, named by its beginning.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p265/r2.anchor: أحدها : أنه عنى به النهار وعبر عنه بالفجر لأنه أوله , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p265/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p265/r3.speaker: علي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p265/r3.claim: It may mean the dawn that begins each day.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p265/r3.anchor: الثاني : أن الفجر الصبح الذي يبدأ به النهار من كل يوم , قاله علي رضي الله عنه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p265/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p265/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p265/r4.claim: It may mean the dawn prayer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p265/r4.anchor: الثالث : أنه عنى به صلاة الصبح , وهو مروي عن ابن عباس أيضا .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p265/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p265/r5.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p265/r5.claim: It may mean specifically the dawn of the day of sacrifice.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p265/r5.anchor: الرابع : أنه أراد به فجر يوم النحر خاصة , قاله مجاهد .

MUJAHID:v2p755/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p755/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MUJAHID:v2p755/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the oath is by the dawn visible in the east, the dawn of day.
MUJAHID:v2p755/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله ﴿ والفجر ﴾ قال هو الفجر الذي ترون من المشرق يقول فجر النهار

MUJAHID:v2p755/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p755/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p755/r2.claim: Mujahid reports the same explanation as Ibn Abbas.
MUJAHID:v2p755/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد مثله

NASAFI-FULL:v4p336/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p336/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p336/r1.claim: The oath is by dawn, meaning morning, as in “the morning when it grows light,” or by the dawn prayer.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p336/r1.anchor: أقسم بالفجر وهو الصبح كقوله والصبح إذا أسفر أو بصلاة الفجر

QURTUBI-FULL:89:1-2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:1-2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:89:1-2/r1.claim: God swears by the dawn; the passage contains five oaths.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:1-2/r1.anchor: أقسم بالفجر. { وليال عشر * والشفع والوتر * والليل إذا يسر } أقسام خمسة.

QURTUBI-FULL:89:1-2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:1-2/r2.speaker: علي وابن الزبير وابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:89:1-2/r2.claim: They say al-fajr is each day's breaking of darkness into daylight.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:1-2/r2.anchor: الفجر هنا: انفجار الظلمة عن النهار من كل يوم قاله علي

QURTUBI-FULL:89:1-2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:1-2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:89:1-2/r3.claim: He also calls the entire day al-fajr because it begins with dawn.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:1-2/r3.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أيضا أنه النهار كله، وعبر عنه بالفجر لأنه أوله.

QURTUBI-FULL:89:1-2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:1-2/r4.speaker: ابن محيصن عن عطية عن ابن عباس وقتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:89:1-2/r4.claim: They identify it as the dawn of the first day of Muharram, from which the year begins to emerge.

QURTUBI-FULL:89:1-2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:1-2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:89:1-2/r5.claim: He also interprets al-fajr as the dawn prayer.

QURTUBI-FULL:89:1-2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:1-2/r6.speaker: ابن جريج عن عطاء عن ابن عباس ومجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:89:1-2/r6.claim: They identify it as the morning of the Day of Sacrifice, arguing each day has a preceding night except that day; pilgrimage remains valid until its dawn.

QURTUBI-FULL:89:1-2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:1-2/r7.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:89:1-2/r7.claim: He says it is the dawn of the day at Jamʿ.

QURTUBI-FULL:89:1-2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:1-2/r8.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
QURTUBI-FULL:89:1-2/r8.claim: He identifies it as the last day of the ten, when pilgrims depart from Jamʿ.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:1-2/r8.anchor: وعن محمد بن كعب القرظي: «والفجر» آخر أيام العشر، إذا دفعت من جمع.

QURTUBI-FULL:89:1-2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:1-2/r9.speaker: الضحاك ومجاهد والسدي والكلبي وابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:89:1-2/r9.claim: They connect al-fajr and the ten nights to the dawn and ten nights of Dhul-Hijja.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:1-2/r9.anchor: وقال الضحاك: فجر ذي الحجة، لأن الله تعالى قرن الأيام به فقال: { وليال عشر } أي ليال عشر من ذي الحجة.

QURTUBI-FULL:89:1-2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:1-2/r11.speaker: أبو الزبير عن جابر عن النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:89:1-2/r11.claim: A Prophetic report interprets the dawn and ten nights as the ten days of sacrifice.

QUTB-ZILAL:89:1/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:89:1/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:89:1/r1.claim: The surah is Meccan and uses varied scenes, rhythms, and rhyme patterns to unite devotional beauty, warning, history, and moral correction.
QUTB-ZILAL:89:1/r1.anchor: السورة من هذا الجانب نموذج واف لهذا الأفق من التناسق الجمالي في التعبير القرآني

QUTB-ZILAL:89:1/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:89:1/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:89:1/r2.claim: The dawn is portrayed as life breathing easily, joyfully, and gently into a waking world, with creation seeming to pray as it opens.
QUTB-ZILAL:89:1/r2.anchor: ساعة تنفس الحياة في يسر ، وفرح ، وابتسام ، وإيناس ودود ندي

RAZI-FULL:v31p147/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p147/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v31p147/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the oath is by ordinary dawn, true and false, whose light ends night, spreads people and animals in search of provision, and offers an image of resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v31p147/r1.anchor: ما روي عن ابن عباس أن الفجر هو الصبح المعروف ، فهو انفجار الصبح الصادق والكاذب

RAZI-FULL:v31p147/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p147/r2.speaker: قوم
RAZI-FULL:v31p147/r2.claim: Some take dawn as the whole day, with its beginning naming the whole, as in oaths by forenoon and daybreak of day.
RAZI-FULL:v31p147/r2.anchor: المراد به جميع النهار إلا أنه دل بالابتداء على الجميع

RAZI-FULL:v31p147/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p147/r3.speaker: قوم
RAZI-FULL:v31p147/r3.claim: Others take it as the Fajr prayer, when night and day angels gather to hear its recitation.
RAZI-FULL:v31p147/r3.anchor: المراد نفسه صلاة الفجر وإنما أقسم بصلاة الفجر

RAZI-FULL:v31p147/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p147/r4.speaker: قوم
RAZI-FULL:v31p147/r4.claim: One specific dawn is Eid al-Adha, when Abrahamic rites and sacrifice occur; the pilgrim's offering recalls the substitute sacrifice in 37:107.
RAZI-FULL:v31p147/r4.anchor: أنه فجر يوم النحر ، وذلك لأن أمر المناسك من خصائص ملة إبراهيم

RAZI-FULL:v31p147/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p147/r5.speaker: قوم
RAZI-FULL:v31p147/r5.claim: Another is dawn of Dhu al-Hijja, paired with the ten nights because the month begins this great pilgrimage worship.
RAZI-FULL:v31p147/r5.anchor: أراد فجر ذي الحجة لأنه قرن به قوله : { وليال عشر }

RAZI-FULL:v31p147/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p147/r6.speaker: قوم
RAZI-FULL:v31p147/r6.claim: Another is dawn of Muharram, the year's first day, associated with recurring yearly rites; a report calls Muharram God's greatest month and Ibn Abbas calls it the year's dawn.
RAZI-FULL:v31p147/r6.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أنه قال : فجر السنة هو المحرم

RAZI-FULL:v31p147/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p147/r7.speaker: قوم
RAZI-FULL:v31p147/r7.claim: A further interpretation is springs of water, whose flowing sustains life.
RAZI-FULL:v31p147/r7.anchor: أنه عنى بالفجر العيون التي تنفجر منها المياه

STUDYQURAN:89:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:intro/r1.speaker: most commentators
STUDYQURAN:89:intro/r1.claim: Most commentators classify al-Fajr as early Makkan, though some call it Madinan; it is probably tenth in revelation order.
STUDYQURAN:89:intro/r1.anchor: though some maintain that it is Madinan

STUDYQURAN:89:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:intro/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:89:intro/r2.claim: The surah's opening oaths lead into accounts of tyrants, human vacillation under fortune, rebuke of stinginess, Judgment Day, and the peaceful believing soul.
STUDYQURAN:89:intro/r2.anchor: The sūrah begins with a series of oaths (vv. 1–4) followed by brief descriptions of the punishments

STUDYQURAN:89:1/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:1/r1.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:89:1/r1.claim: Some take the dawn and ten nights as the beginning of Muḥarram and its first ten nights.
STUDYQURAN:89:1/r1.anchor: Some see these verses as a reference to the break of dawn at the beginning of Muḥarram

STUDYQURAN:89:1/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:1/r2.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:89:1/r2.claim: Others identify the dawn with the Feast of Sacrifice and the ten nights with the first ten of Dhu’l-Ḥijjah.
STUDYQURAN:89:1/r2.anchor: Others see them as a reference to the break of dawn at the Feast of Sacrifice

STUDYQURAN:89:1/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:1/r3.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:89:1/r3.claim: Another interpretation points to dawn during Ramadan and its last ten nights, when the Quran was first revealed.
STUDYQURAN:89:1/r3.anchor: Others see them as a reference to the break of dawn during Ramadan and the last ten nights of Ramadan

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-4:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-4:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-4:anmerkung/r1.claim: Qur'anic oath formulas probably draw on a characteristic expression of pre-Islamic soothsayers, though this connection remains insufficiently studied.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-4:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Zu grundsätzlichen Hinweisen zu den koranischen Schwüren sowie ihrer wahrscheinlichen, aber bis dato noch nicht hinreichend untersuchten Anlehnung an ein charakteristisches Ausdrucksmittel altarabischer Seher

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-4:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-4:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-4:anmerkung/r2.claim: For the oath type in this passage, the commentary directs readers to its discussion of 93:1–2.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-4:anmerkung/r2.anchor: zum hier vorliegenden Schwurtypus s. die Anmerkung zu 93:1.2

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-2:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-2:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-2:anmerkung/r1.claim: Across parallel oaths, dawn or day is contrasted with night; the ten nights vary this same contrast and uniquely quantify the night.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-2:anmerkung/r1.anchor: In all diesen Parallelstellen werden der Morgen bzw. der Tag mit der Nacht kontrastiert; wenn in 89:1.2 als Schwurgegenstände der Tagesanbruch und die „zehn Nächte“ genannt werden, so handelt es sich dabei um eine Variation desselben Kontrasts.

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-2:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-2:anmerkung/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-2:anmerkung/r3.claim: Despite objections to Neuwirth's liturgical reading of cosmic oath series, a cultic interpretation of the ten nights is persuasive.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-2:anmerkung/r3.anchor: ist eine kultische Deutung der in V. 2 genannten „zehn Nächte“ doch einleuchtend

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-2:anmerkung/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-2:anmerkung/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-2:anmerkung/r4.claim: The passage foregrounds cosmic duality—dawn and night, odd and even—which elsewhere aligns with moral good and evil and their eschatological recompense.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-2:anmerkung/r4.anchor: das insbesondere in Schwurpassagen aus Gruppe II prominente Motiv kosmischer Dualität (Tagesanbruch – Nacht, gerade – ungerade) im Vordergrund

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-2:anmerkung/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-2:anmerkung/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-2:anmerkung/r5.claim: A likely authentic poem by Umayya b. abī ṣ-Ṣalt supports a cultic or liturgical connotation for dawn, opening with a greeting to the Lord at each dawn.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-2:anmerkung/r5.anchor: ein sehr wahrscheinlich authentisches Gedicht Umayya b. abī ṣ-Ṣalts mit den Worten „Sei gegrüsst, Herr, bei jeder Morgendämmerung (faǧr) …“ beginnt

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-5:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-5:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-5:kommentar/r1.claim: The opening oath resembles those in earlier suras 93, 95, 100, and 103 and roughly contemporary suras 91 and 92.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-5:kommentar/r1.anchor: Die Sure setzt mit einer Schwureinleitung ein, wie sie bereits in den früheren Suren 93, 95, 100 und 103 und den in etwa gleichzeitigen Suren 91 und 92 erscheint

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-5:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-5:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-5:kommentar/r2.claim: The oath's cosmic oppositions, day/night and odd/even, resemble 91 and 92, where such duality anticipates moral and afterlife oppositions.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-5:kommentar/r2.anchor: Wie in Q 91, 92 und 93 ist in der Schwurpassage ein Tag-Nacht-Gegensatz zentral

TABATABAI:89:1-3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:89:1-3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:89:1-3/r1.claim: The surah condemns attachment to worldly life, which leads to tyranny and ingratitude: people mistake wealth for divine favor and poverty for humiliation, though both are tests of what they prepare for the afterlife.
TABATABAI:89:1-3/r1.anchor: فما يصيبه من القدرة والثروة ومن الفقر وضيق المعاش امتحان وابتلاء إلهي

TABATABAI:89:1-3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:89:1-3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:89:1-3/r2.claim: At judgment people will realize that wealth, poverty, power, and weakness were tests; they could prepare for the next life but chose punishment over reward.
TABATABAI:89:1-3/r2.anchor: وكان يمكنه أن يقدم من يومه لغده فلم يفعل وآثر العقاب على الثواب

TABATABAI:89:1-3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:89:1-3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:89:1-3/r3.claim: Salvation belongs to the tranquil soul submitted to God, steady through trials and neither tyrannized by gain nor made ungrateful by loss; the surah is Meccan by its context.
TABATABAI:89:1-3/r3.anchor: التي لا تتزلزل بعواصف الابتلاءات ولا يطغيه الوجدان ولا يكفره الفقدان

TABATABAI:89:1-3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:89:1-3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:89:1-3/r4.claim: Fajr is dawn, shafʿ is an even pair, witr is odd, the night passes and withdraws, and ḥijr means intellect; the oath invokes dawn and the following objects.
TABATABAI:89:1-3/r4.anchor: الفجر الصبح والشفع الزوج، قال الراغب الشفع ضم الشيء إلى مثله

TABATABAI:89:1-3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:89:1-3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:89:1-3/r5.claim: Fajr most likely means dawn generally, though it may mean the dawn of the tenth of Dhu al-Hijjah; proposals include the month's dawn, Muharram, Friday, Muzdalifah, prayer, all daylight, or springs, which the author calls poor.
TABATABAI:89:1-3/r5.anchor: ولعل ظاهر قوله { والفجر } أن المراد به مطلق الفجر

TABRISI:89:1-30#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:1-30#3/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:89:1-30#3/r1.claim: The oath's response is “Your Lord is surely watching”; another proposed response is implicit: He will seize oppressors or vindicate the wronged.
TABRISI:89:1-30#3/r1.anchor: جواب القسم قوله { إن ربك لبالمرصاد }

TABRISI:89:1-30#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:1-30#3/r6.speaker: عكرمة والحسن والجبائي وأبو صالح عن ابن عباس
TABRISI:89:1-30#3/r6.claim: They interpret dawn as the daily breaking of morning light.
TABRISI:89:1-30#3/r6.anchor: أقسم الله سبحانه بفجر النهار وهو انفجار الصبح كل يوم عن عكرمة

TABRISI:89:1-30#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:1-30#3/r7.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك
TABRISI:89:1-30#3/r7.claim: They identify the dawn as that of Dhu al-Hijja, paired with the ten nights.
TABRISI:89:1-30#3/r7.anchor: وقيل: هو فجر ذي الحجة لأن الله تعالى قرن الأيام به

TABRISI:89:1-30#3/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:1-30#3/r8.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:89:1-30#3/r8.claim: Qatada identifies the dawn as the first of Muharram, when a new year begins.
TABRISI:89:1-30#3/r8.anchor: فجر أول المحرم لأنه تتجدد عنده السنة عن قتادة

TABRISI:89:1-30#3/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:1-30#3/r9.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:89:1-30#3/r9.claim: Abu Muslim says it is the dawn of the Sacrifice Day, when the offering occurs and the ten nights culminate.
TABRISI:89:1-30#3/r9.anchor: يريد فجر يوم النحر لأنه يقع فيه القربان ويتصل بالليالي العشر عن أبي مسلم

TABRISI:89:1-30#3/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:1-30#3/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:89:1-30#3/r10.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas interprets dawn as the whole day.
TABRISI:89:1-30#3/r10.anchor: وقيل: أراد بالفجر النهار كله عن ابن عباس

THALABI:v10p191#3/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p191#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p191#3/r1.claim: He interprets dawn as the whole daytime.
THALABI:v10p191#3/r1.anchor: والفجر قال ابن عباس: يعني النهار كله

THALABI:v10p191#3/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p191#3/r2.speaker: عطية عن ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p191#3/r2.claim: He transmits the interpretation that dawn means the dawn prayer.

THALABI:v10p191#3/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p191#3/r3.speaker: عثمان بن محصن
THALABI:v10p191#3/r3.claim: He interprets it as the dawn of Muharram; Qatada gives the same view and calls it the year's first day.
THALABI:v10p191#3/r3.anchor: عثمان بن محصن عنه: فجر المحرم ومثله قال قتادة: هو أول يوم من المحرم تتفجر منه السنة

THALABI:v10p191#3/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p191#3/r4.speaker: ضحاك
THALABI:v10p191#3/r4.claim: He identifies dawn as that of Dhu al-Hijja, since God connects the oath to those days.
THALABI:v10p191#3/r4.anchor: ضحاك: فجر ذي الحجة لأن الله سبحانه قرن الأيام بها

THALABI:v10p191#3/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p191#3/r5.speaker: عكرمة وزيد بن أسلم
THALABI:v10p191#3/r5.claim: They interpret it as morning light.

THALABI:v10p191#3/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p191#3/r6.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v10p191#3/r6.claim: He interprets it as the beginning of every year.

THALABI:v10p191#3/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p191#3/r7.speaker: القرظي
THALABI:v10p191#3/r7.claim: He says it is daybreak each day until the end of the world.
THALABI:v10p191#3/r7.anchor: القرظي: انفجار الصبح من كل يوم إلى انقضاء الدنيا

THALABI:v10p191#3/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p191#3/r8.speaker: بعض التفاسير
THALABI:v10p191#3/r8.claim: Some commentaries take fajr as rocks and springs bursting with water.
THALABI:v10p191#3/r8.anchor: في بعض التفاسير: أن الفجر الصخور والعيون تتفجر بالمياه

THALABI:v10p191#3/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p191#3/r15.speaker: عطية العوفي عن أبي سعيد الخدري عن النبي
THALABI:v10p191#3/r15.claim: A report identifies the dawn as the familiar dawn, the ten nights as the ten of sacrifice, the even as creation, and the odd as God.
THALABI:v10p191#3/r15.anchor: عن عطية العوفي في قوله سبحانه: والفجر قال: هو الفجر الذي تعرفون، قلت: وليال عشر قال: عشر الأضحى

THALABI:v10p192/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p192/r1.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله عن النبي
THALABI:v10p192/r1.claim: The Prophet explains the ten as the ten of sacrifice, the odd as the Day of Arafat, and the even as the Day of Sacrifice.
THALABI:v10p192/r1.anchor: عشر النحر، والوتر يوم عرفة، والشفع يوم النحر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p483#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p483#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو نصر وأبو صالح
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p483#2/r1.claim: They interpret al-fajr as the dawn of the day.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p483#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: فجر النهار. وهو رواية أبى نصر (¬2) (¬3)، # وأبي صالح (¬1)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p483#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p483#2/r2.speaker: عكرمة وزيد بن أسلم ومحمد بن كعب والأسود بن يزيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p483#2/r2.claim: They take it as the rising light of every morning.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p483#2/r2.anchor: وقول عكرمة (¬2)، (وزيد بن أسلم (¬3)) (¬4)، ومحمد بن كعب (¬5)، (والأسود بن يزيد (¬6) (¬7)، قالوا: هو انفجار الصبح من كل يوم) (¬8)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p483#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p483#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية العوفي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p483#2/r3.claim: He interprets it as the dawn prayer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p483#2/r3.anchor: وقال في رواية العوفي: صلاة الفجر (¬9)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p483#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p483#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية عثمان بن محيصن وقتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p483#2/r4.claim: They identify it as the first dawn of Muharram; Qatada says God swore by the first day of the year.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p483#2/r4.anchor: وقال في رواية عثمان (¬10) بن محيصن (¬11) هو (¬12): فجر المحرم (¬13)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p483#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p483#2/r5.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p483#2/r5.claim: He says it is the morning of the day of sacrifice.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p483#2/r5.anchor: وقال في رواية عطاء: يريد صبيحة يوم النحر (¬2)

WAHIDI-QT:89:1/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:89:1/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:89:1/r1.claim: Al-fajr means the dawn of every day.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:1-6/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:1-6/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:1-6/r1.claim: The oath by dawn means every day's dawn.

ELMALILI:89:1-3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:1-3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:1-3/r1.claim: The opening oaths direct attention to temporal events that show worldly change, move from darkness to light and grief to joy, and indicate the Creator’s lordship.
ELMALILI:89:1-3/r1.anchor: âlemdeki inkılâbâta delâlet eyleyen ve insanı zulmetten nûra, kederden sürûra götüren

ELMALILI:89:1-3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:1-3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:1-3/r2.claim: Commentators offer many views on the definite or indefinite wording, the scope of the articles, and the identification and interpretation of the oath objects.
ELMALILI:89:1-3/r2.anchor: Bunların ta‘rîf ve tenkirlerine ve “lâm”larındaki ahid veya cins veya istiğrak ihtimalleri itibariyle

ELMALILI:89:1-3#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:1-3#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:1-3#2/r1.claim: Fajr is the first whiteness as night darkness breaks: the false dawn is vertical and the true dawn horizontal; fasting and prayer rulings attach only to the true dawn.
ELMALILI:89:1-3#2/r1.anchor: “Fecr” mâlum ki gece karanlığının çatladığı sabahın ilk beyazlığıdır

ELMALILI:89:1-3#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:1-3#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:1-3#2/r2.claim: Dawn is the joyful instant when the world begins moving from darkness into light, so the generic dawn is a meaningful oath, as in 81:18.
ELMALILI:89:1-3#2/r2.anchor: Bu suretle fecir, cihânın zulmetten nûra geçmek üzere gülümsediği en neş’eli, mes‘ud bir demidir.

ELMALILI:89:1-3#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:1-3#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:1-3#2/r3.claim: Some take the article as specific and understand the dawn of a blessed Friday or feast; Mujahid’s reported view most immediately points to the tenth of Dhul Hijjah, the Adha feast day.
ELMALILI:89:1-3#2/r3.anchor: Bu surette[^3] en mütebâdiri Mücâhid’den mervî olduğu üzere kurban bayramı gününün fecri olmaktır

ELMALILI:89:1-3#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:1-3#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:1-3#2/r4.claim: Although generic dawn includes the feast dawn, the particular dawn more strongly conveys the collective joy of the occasion.
ELMALILI:89:1-3#2/r4.anchor: Evvelki buna dahi şâmil olursa da bunda daha ziyade bir hususiyet ve cem‘iyyet ile sürûra işaret vardır.

ELMALILI:89:1-3#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:1-3#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:1-3#2/r10.claim: Jabir reports from the Prophet that the oath’s dawn and ten nights refer to the Adha ten; al-Tabari says this is correct because the authorities of interpretation agree.
ELMALILI:89:1-3#2/r10.anchor: Hazret-i Câbir’den de “Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem عَشْرُ الأَْضْحَى,وَٱلْفَجْرِ وَلَيَالٍ عَشْرٍۢ’dır buyurdu” diye merfû‘an rivayet etmişlerdir.

ELMALILI:89:1-3#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:1-3#3/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:1-3#3/r11.claim: The reports identifying Dhul Hijjah’s nights, Arafah, and the sacrifice day best fit the sequence and surah’s purpose, include the possible senses, and urge worship during life’s limited span to attain afterlife joy.
ELMALILI:89:1-3#3/r11.anchor: Ma‘amâfîh Câbir ve İbn [5797] Abbas rivayetleri üzere aşr-i zilhicce geceleri ve arefe

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:1/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:1/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:1/r1.claim: Fajr means dawn breaking, morning brightness, or the time of daybreak.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:1/r1.anchor: fecr kelimesi masdar olarak “tan yerinin ağarması”, isim olarak belirttiğimiz anlamı yanında, “sabah aydınlığı, şafak vakti, tan yerinin ağarma zamanı” gibi anlamlara gelmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:1/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:1/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:1/r2.claim: Dawn's light and the waking of living things resemble resurrection; God swears by it to direct attention to what follows (cf. al-Takwir 81:18).
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:1/r2.anchor: Tan yerinin ağarma zamanı ortalığın aydınlanmaya, canlıların da uyanmaya başlaması, bir çeşit yeniden dirilmeye benzediği için yüce Allah sabah aydınlığına yemin ederek aşağıda anlatılacak konulara dikkat çekmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:1/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:1/r10.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:1/r10.claim: The unstated oath's answer is taken either to affirm resurrection, Judgment, punishment, and reward, or to be verse 14: God watches all, knows deeds, and recompenses them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:1/r10.anchor: Müfessirlere göre Allah Teâlâ bu dört âyette kendi katında önemli olan varlıklara yemin ederek öldükten sonra dirilme, kıyamet, hesap, ceza ve mükâfatın gerçekleşeceğini vurgulamıştır

QASHANI:89:2-3/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:89:2-3/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:89:2-3/r3.claim: Alternatively, the oaths describe the great resurrection: dawn is divine light appearing in the soul’s night; ten are dormant senses during self-disclosure; the pair is witness and witnessed before complete annihilation; the odd is the oneness after duality ends; night is selfhood disappearing.
QASHANI:89:2-3/r3.anchor: الفجر الذي هو مبتدأ طلوع نور الحق وتأثيره في ليلة النفس وليال عشر من الحواس الراكدة الهادئة المظلمة

QASHANI:89:2-3/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:89:2-3/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:89:2-3/r4.claim: A second alternative is the lesser resurrection of death: dawn is the sun rising from the west, the ten are dimmed senses, the pair spirit and body, the odd the separated spirit, and night the body’s darkness dispersing.
QASHANI:89:2-3/r4.anchor: أي: فجر ابتداء ظهور نور الشمس الطالعة من مغربها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p313/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p313/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p313/r1.claim: Al-fajr most likely means dawn generically, fitting its coordination with night; it may instead mean each day's dawn per Qatada, or the sacrifice-day dawn at Muzdalifah per Ibn Abbas, Ata, and Ikrima.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p313/r1.anchor: فالتعريف في { الفجر } تعريف الجنس وهو الأظهر لمناسبة عطف { والليل إذا يسر } .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p313/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p313/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p313/r5.claim: The dawn ends the night, so their opposition unites the oath; the ten blessed nights are singled out as a subset of night.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p313/r5.anchor: ومناسبة عطف { ليال عشر } على { الفجر } أن الفجر وقت انتهاء الليل ، فبينه وبين الليل جامع المضادة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p390#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p390#2/r1.speaker: علي وابن عباس ومجاهد وعكرمة والسدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p390#2/r1.claim: They say al-fajr is the morning dawn.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p390#2/r1.anchor: أما الفجر فمعروف، وهو: الصبح. قاله علي، وابن عباس، ومجاهد، وعكرمة، والسدي.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p390#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p390#2/r2.speaker: مسروق ومجاهد ومحمد بن كعب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p390#2/r2.claim: They restrict the dawn to the dawn of the Day of Sacrifice, the close of the ten nights.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p390#2/r2.anchor: وعن مسروق، ومجاهد، ومحمد بن كعب: المراد به فجر يوم النحر خاصة، وهو خاتمة الليالي العشر.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p390#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p390#2/r3.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p390#2/r3.claim: ʿIkrima says the oath refers to the prayer performed at dawn.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p390#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: المراد بذلك الصلاة التي تفعل عنده، كما قاله عكرمة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p390#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p390#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p390#2/r4.claim: One report from Ibn ʿAbbās says dawn refers to the whole day.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p390#2/r4.anchor: وقيل: المراد به جميع النهار. وهو رواية عن ابن عباس.

JISHUMI:v10p7396/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7396/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7396/r5.claim: Fajr means breaking the column of dawn; two dawns are distinguished: the elongated false dawn remains legally night, but the spreading true dawn governs fasting and prayer.
JISHUMI:v10p7396/r5.anchor: الفجر: شق عمود الصبح، فجره الله تعالى

JISHUMI:v10p7402/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r1.claim: The dawn oath and what follows highlight the great value of these signs and blessings as evidence for the Creator.
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r1.anchor: يدل قوله: (والفجر) وما بعده على عظيم موقع هذه الأشياء من النعمة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p748/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p748/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p748/r2.claim: Surat al-Fajr is Meccan; the source gives its length as thirty verses, with an alternative count of twenty-nine, and says it followed Surat al-Layl.

TAB-FULL:v24p344#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p344#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p344#2/r1.claim: One report from Ibn ʿAbbās interprets al-fajr as daytime.
TAB-FULL:v24p344#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {والفجر} [الفجر: 1] قال: النهار

TAB-FULL:v24p344#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p344#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p344#2/r2.claim: Another Ibn ʿAbbās report identifies al-fajr as the dawn prayer.
TAB-FULL:v24p344#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {والفجر} [الفجر: 1] يعني: صلاة الفجر

TAB-FULL:v24p344#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p344#2/r3.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v24p344#2/r3.claim: ʿIkrima says al-fajr means the dawn itself.
TAB-FULL:v24p344#2/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة، في قوله: {والفجر} [الفجر: 1] قال: الفجر: فجر الصبح

TAB-FULL:v24p344#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p344#2/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبير
TAB-FULL:v24p344#2/r4.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says God has sworn by al-fajr.
TAB-FULL:v24p344#2/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن الزبير، أنه قال: {والفجر} [الفجر: 1] قال: الفجر: قسم أقسم الله به

ZAJJAJ:v5p321/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p321/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p321/r1.claim: Al-fajr is dawn breaking out of night, and the oath's answer is that God watches in ambush.
ZAJJAJ:v5p321/r1.anchor: الفجر انفجار الصبح من الليل، وجواب القسم (إن ربك لبالمرصاد (14)

TABRISI:89:29/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:29/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:89:29/r1.claim: Fajr is the cleaving of dawn's vertical light, announcing the departure of dark night and arrival of bright day; the source distinguishes the false vertical dawn from true spread dawn.
TABRISI:89:29/r1.anchor: الفجر شق عمود الصبح فجره الله لعباده فجرا إذا أظهره في أفق المشرق

ALUSI-FULL:v30p118#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p118#2/r7.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v30p118#2/r7.claim: The Fajr sūrah is Meccan according to most interpreters, though ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭalḥah says it is Medinan; verse counts vary by regional enumeration.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p118#2/r7.anchor: مكية في قول الجمهور وقال علي بن أبي طلحة مدنية وآيها اثنتان وثلاثون آية في الحجازي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p118#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p118#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p118#2/r8.claim: The sūrah follows Ghāshiya's two kinds of faces by describing the arrogant deniers, then the blessed class through “O tranquil soul”; al-Suyūṭī sees its opening oath as affirming the previous sūrah's promise and threat and notes the parallel opening questions.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p118#2/r8.anchor: ولما ذكر سبحانه فيما قبلها وجوه يومئذ خاشعة ووجوه يومئذ ناعمة أتبعه تعالى بذكر الطوائف المكذبين

BINTSHATI:v2p127/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p127/r1.speaker: ابن قيم الجوزية
BINTSHATI:v2p127/r1.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim suggests that the dawn is the dawn of Dhū al-Ḥijja, based on the following oath by ten nights.
BINTSHATI:v2p127/r1.anchor: أو هو فجر ذي الحجة، لقوله تعالى بعده: {وَلَيَالٍ عَشْرٍ} كما في (التبيان) لابن قيم الجوزية.

BINTSHATI:v2p129/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p129/r6.speaker: الشيخ محمد عبده
BINTSHATI:v2p129/r6.claim: Muḥammad ʿAbduh takes the ten as nights at the start of every month and similarly understands dawn generically.
BINTSHATI:v2p129/r6.anchor: واختار الشيخ محمد عبده أن تكون عشر ليال من أول كل شهر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p413/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p413/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p413/r1.claim: The Fajr sura's purpose is to support the return and reckoning mentioned at the end of Ghashiya: dawn's emergence resembles sleepers returning from death-like sleep to daytime work for reward or punishment.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p413/r1.anchor: مقصودها الاستدلال على آخر الغاشية الإياب والحساب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p413/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p413/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p413/r2.claim: The basmala depicts God gathering servants after dispersal through divine majesty, giving them clarifying guidance, and granting the chosen their gardens through mercy.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p413/r2.anchor: جامع العباد بعد تمزيقهم بما له من العظمة

DURR-FULL:v8p500/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p500/r10.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
DURR-FULL:v8p500/r10.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet identifies the ten as the ten of sacrifice, the pair with “We created you in pairs,” and the odd as God.
DURR-FULL:v8p500/r10.anchor: عن عطية في قوله: {والفجر} قال: هذا الذي تعرفون {وليال عشر} قال: عشر الأضحى

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p154/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
