BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p154/r1.speaker: الرازي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p154/r1.claim: Al-Rāzī explains that a sūra mentioning the Qur’an thereby draws attention to all of it; other opening forms suit hearts not occupied by anything besides the Qur’an, and the openings of al-Ḥajj and al-Taḥrīm invoke great matters.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p154/r1.anchor: وقد رد الرازي على الأول، بأن السورة التي فيها ذكر القرآن

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p154/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p154/r2.speaker: الرازي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p154/r2.claim: Al-Rāzī attributes the absence of a later Qur’an reference in some letter-opened sūras to the weight of the Qur’an’s obligations and meanings.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p154/r2.anchor: وأما السور التي افتتحت بالحروف ولم يذكر بعدها القرآن أو التنزيل، فعلَّله بأن ثقل القرآن، بما فيه من التكاليف والمعاني

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p154/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p154/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p154/r3.claim: The author finds al-Rāzī’s explanations unconvincing and plainly forced.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p154/r3.anchor: ولا يبدو ردهُّ مقنعاً، بل هو واضح التكلف

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p154/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p154/r4.speaker: الزركشي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p154/r4.claim: Al-Zarkashī notes the usual pattern of mentioning the Qur’an after disjoint letters and asks why al-ʿAnkabūt and al-Rūm differ.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p154/r4.anchor: واعلم أن عادة القرآن العظيم في ذكر هذه الحروف، أن يذكر بعدها ما يتعلق بالقرآن

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p154/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p154/r5.speaker: ابن كثير
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p154/r5.claim: Ibn Kathīr’s inductive answer is that every sūra opened with disjoint letters includes a defense of the Qur’an and a demonstration of its inimitability.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p154/r5.anchor: فهداه الاستقراء إلى أن كل سورة افتتحت بالحروف فلابد أن يذكر فيها الانتصار للقرآن وبيان إعجازه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p244/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p244/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p244/r1.claim: Wāw normally links clauses, but as an oath it comes first to authenticate what is denied or to mark acknowledgment and testimony.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p244/r1.anchor: والأصل في الواو أن تأتي في درَج الكلام للربط والعطف، فإذا جاءت للقسم فإن لها الصدارة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p244/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p244/r2.speaker: المفسرون
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p244/r2.claim: Most exegetes take oath-wāw as magnifying the object sworn by and seek the source of its greatness.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p244/r2.anchor: وقد اتجه بها المفسرون، أو جمهرتهم فيما أعلم، إلى تعظيم المقسَم به

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p244/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p244/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p244/r3.claim: She argues that perceiving a purpose in a created thing does not establish its greatness, and that exegetes often overlook restrictions such as ‘when it settles’ or ‘when it falls.’
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p244/r3.anchor: وأكثر ما ذكروه من ذلك يدخل في الحكمة وهي تختلف تماماً عن العظمة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p245/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p245/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p245/r2.claim: She asks what rhetorical effect oath-wāw has and whether an Arab listener perceived a difference between that form and an explicit ‘I swear by’ construction.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p245/r2.anchor: وبين مألوف التعبير بصريح القسم: أقسم بالضحى، وبالليل إذا سجى، وأقسم بالنجم إذا هوى؟

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p245/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p245/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p245/r3.claim: She observes that sūras opening with oath-wāw are all Meccan; no Medinan sūra begins with it.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p245/r3.anchor: وكلها سور مكية، ولم تأت سورة مدنية مبدوءة بهذه الواو

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p260/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p260/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p260/r1.claim: The cited account calls endings eloquent when they arise easily from the meaning, but rejects making the meaning follow a forced sound pattern; it cites matching endings in Ṭā Hā, al-Ṭūr, al-ʿĀdiyāt, and al-Fajr, including deletion of final yāʾ in the latter.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p260/r1.anchor: يكون يأتي طوعاً سهلاً وتابعاً للمعاني، وبالضد من ذلك حتى يكون متكلفاً يتبعه المعنى

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p260/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p260/r2.speaker: الرماني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p260/r2.claim: Al-Rummānī distinguishes matching endings, which he allows calling sajʿ, from merely near endings, but the author rejects his blanket claim that sajʿ is defective while Qur’anic fawāṣil are eloquent.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p260/r2.anchor: فأما قول الرومانى: "إن السجع عيب والفواصل بلاغة" على الإطلاق، فغلط

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p260/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p260/r3.speaker: الخفاجي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p260/r3.claim: Al-Khafājī suggests scholars called all Qur’anic endings fawāṣil, even when they rhyme, to keep the Qur’an from an associated description.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p260/r3.anchor: وأظن أن الذي دعا اصحابنا إلى تسمية كل ما في القرآن فواصل، ولم يسموا ما تماثلت حروفه سجعاً

NASHR:v1p216/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p216/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p216/r1.claim: The passage rejects the claim that Warsh's alifs in طال and فصال are light: their position between emphatic letters prevents that, and confusing قال with حال shows poor articulation.
NASHR:v1p216/r1.anchor: والدليل على جهله أنه يدعي أن الألف في قراءة ورش طال وفصالا وما أشبههما مرققة وترقيقها غير ممكن

NASHR:v1p216/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p216/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p216/r2.claim: Most grammarians explicitly recognize emphatic alif; Abu Hayyan praised the cited author's learning and the quality of his evidence.
NASHR:v1p216/r2.anchor: والدليل على عدم اطلاعه أن أكثر النحاة نصوا في كتبهم على تفخيم الألف

NASHR:v1p216/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p216/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p216/r3.claim: When beginning a word, pronounce hamza smoothly and avoid harshness, especially before alif, emphatic letters, or matching and nearby letters; the closer the following sound, the more care needed.
NASHR:v1p216/r3.anchor: فالهمزة - إذا ابتدأ بها القارئ من كلمة فليلفظ بها سلسة في النطق سهلة في الذوق

NASHR:v1p216/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p216/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p216/r4.claim: Keep bāʾ light before emphatics, with extra care when an alif intervenes or two emphatics follow; preserve the strength of its lightness even in lighter or weak contexts.
NASHR:v1p216/r4.anchor: وكذا الباء: إذا أتى بعدها حرف مفخم نحو بطل، بغى، وبصلها، فإن حال بينهما ألف كان التحفظ بترقيقها أبلغ

NASHR:v1p216/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p216/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p216/r5.claim: When bāʾ is quiescent, preserve its plosive strength and voiced quality; this is also the rule for the other qalqala letters, which combine strength and voicing.
NASHR:v1p216/r5.anchor: وإذا سكنت كان التحفظ بما فيها من الشدة والجهر أشد نحو: ربوة، و (الخبء)

NASHR:v1p216/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p216/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p216/r6.claim: The qalqala letters share shidda and jahr; al-fajr is among the examples illustrating this articulation rule.
NASHR:v1p216/r6.anchor: وكذلك) الحكم في سائر حروف القلقلة لاجتماع الشدة والجهر فيها نحو: (يجعلون، والحجر، والفجر

NASHR:v1p261#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p261#2/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p261#2/r1.claim: Among readers of Hamza, Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, Yaʿqub, and Warsh who join surahs, many choose a brief pause at four specified transitions, including Fajr and Asr.
NASHR:v1p261#2/r1.anchor: اختار كثير منهم لهم السكت بين (المدثر، ولا أقسم بيوم القيامة - وبين - الانفطار وويل للمصلين

NASHR:v1p261#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p261#2/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p261#2/r2.claim: Many of the same named readers who pause generally choose basmala at the four transitions; the author lists Ibn Ghalbun, the Hidaya author, Makki, and others.
NASHR:v1p261#2/r2.anchor: وكذا الآخذون بالسكت لمن ذكر من أبي عمرو، وابن عامر، ويعقوب، وورش، اختار كثير منهم لهم البسملة

NASHR:v1p261#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p261#2/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p261#2/r3.claim: They separate the joins to avoid jarring phrases such as أهل المغفرة لا, ادخلي جنتي لا, لله ويل, and وتواصوا بالصبر ويل.
NASHR:v1p261#2/r3.anchor: وإنما اختاروا ذلك لبشاعة وقوع مثل ذلك إذا قيل: (أهل المغفرة لا) أو: (ادخلي جنتي لا)

NASHR:v1p261#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p261#2/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p261#2/r4.claim: Readers who join cannot insert basmala where explicit transmission excludes it, since that would oppose the transmitted reading with a discretionary choice.
NASHR:v1p261#2/r4.anchor: ولم يمكنهم البسملة له ; لأنه ثبت عنه النص بعدم البسملة، فلو بسملوا لصادموا النص بالاختيار

NASHR:v1p261#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p261#2/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p261#2/r5.claim: Most authorities make no special distinction for these four transitions; this is the position of Faris ibn Ahmad, Ibn Sufyan, Abu al-Tahir, the Iraqis, al-Dani, and other investigators.
NASHR:v1p261#2/r5.anchor: والأكثرون على عدم التفرقة بين الأربعة وغيرها

NASHR:v1p261#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p261#2/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p261#2/r6.claim: The special treatment derives from the reader's general practice: special sakt means joining elsewhere, while special basmala means pausing elsewhere; no one transmits basmala for those who join.
NASHR:v1p261#2/r6.anchor: تخصيص السكت والبسملة في الأربعة المذكورة مفرع على الوصل والسكت مطلقا

NASHR:v1p334#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p334#2/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p334#2/r1.claim: Ibn al-Fahham alone transmits from Hisham, through al-Farisi and the al-Zaydi line, a full extension in both of the two types under discussion, contrary to the other transmitters.
NASHR:v1p334#2/r1.anchor: وقد انفرد أبو القاسم بن الفحام في " التجريد " عن الفارسي، عن الشريف الزيدي، عن النقاش، عن الحلواني، عن هشام بإشباع المد

NASHR:v1p334#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p334#2/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p334#2/r2.claim: If connected length is not differentiated, it takes full extension like the highest separate-length degree; otherwise separate length would wrongly be preferred. Accordingly, necessary-sukun madd is fully extended.
NASHR:v1p334#2/r2.anchor: من ذهب إلى عدم تفاوت المتصل، فإنه يأخذ فيه الإشباع كأعلى مراتب المنفصل

NASHR:v1p334#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p334#2/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
NASHR:v1p334#2/r3.claim: One view fully extends at incidental sukun, treating the two sukuns as meeting; al-Dani attributes it to early Egyptian shaykhs and says he used it when stopping with al-Khaqani. The author notes Shatibi and others chose it too.
NASHR:v1p334#2/r3.anchor: الإشباع كاللازم لاجتماع الساكنين اعتدادا بالعارض. قال الداني: وهو مذهب القدماء من مشيخة المصريين

NASHR:v1p334#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p334#2/r4.speaker: أبو بكر بن مجاهد
NASHR:v1p334#2/r4.claim: A second view uses medium length, recognizing both the two sukuns and the accidental nature of the pause; Ibn Mujahid and his students held it, as did al-Dani and others. It is assigned to several readers and routes.
NASHR:v1p334#2/r4.anchor: التوسط لمراعاة اجتماع الساكنين وملاحظة كونه عارضا. وهو مذهب أبي بكر بن مجاهد

NASHR:v1p334#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p334#2/r5.speaker: أبو الحسن علي بن عبد الغني الحصري
NASHR:v1p334#2/r5.claim: A third view shortens the madd because the stopping sukun is incidental and should not count; its proponent says meeting two sukuns is specific to stopping, as in al-qadr and al-fajr.
NASHR:v1p334#2/r5.anchor: وهو مذهب أبي الحسن علي بن عبد الغني الحصري

NASHR:v2p99/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p99/r1.speaker: أبو الحسن طاهر بن غلبون
NASHR:v2p99/r1.claim: For a damma raa occurring medially or finally after kasra or silent ya, or separated from kasra by a consonant, some transmitters preserve tafkhim; Abu al-Hasan Tahir ibn Ghalbun and others take this view.
NASHR:v2p99/r1.anchor: فروى بعضهم تفخيمها في ذلك، ولم يجروها مجرى المفتوحة. وهذا مذهب أبي الحسن طاهر بن غلبون

NASHR:v2p99/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p99/r2.speaker: جمهورهم
NASHR:v2p99/r2.claim: Most transmitters instead apply tarqiq in those environments; al-Dani read it from al-Khaqani and Abu al-Fath and reports it from the general Warsh performance tradition in Egypt and the Maghreb.
NASHR:v2p99/r2.anchor: جمهورهم ترقيقها، وهو الذي في التيسير والهادي، والكافي

NASHR:v2p99/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p99/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p99/r3.claim: Ibn al-Jazari judges tarqiq the soundest position by textual evidence, transmission, and analogy.
NASHR:v2p99/r3.anchor: والترقيق هو الأصح نصا ورواية وقياسا - والله أعلم -

NASHR:v2p99/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p99/r4.speaker: أبو محمد صاحب التبصرة
NASHR:v2p99/r4.claim: The transmitters who favored tarqiq disagree over عشرون and كبر ما هم ببالغيه: Abu Muhammad, al-Mahdawi, Ibn Sufyan, and the Tajrid author use tafkhim.
NASHR:v2p99/r4.anchor: ففخمها منهم أبو محمد صاحب التبصرة، والمهدوي وابن سفيان، وصاحب التجريد

NASHR:v2p99/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p99/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
NASHR:v2p99/r5.claim: For the same two words, al-Dani, his teachers, Abu Maʿshar, Ibn Buleyma, al-Shatibi, and others use tarqiq.
NASHR:v2p99/r5.anchor: ورققها أبو عمرو الداني وشيخاه أبو الفتح والخاقاني وأبو معشر الطبري

NASHR:v2p99/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p99/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p99/r6.claim: A raa bearing kasra is light for every reader without disagreement; al-fajr is among the examples when final raa bears kasra in connected speech.
NASHR:v2p99/r6.anchor: وأما الراء المكسورة فإنها مرققة لجميع القراء من غير خلف عن أحد منهم

NASHR:v2p110/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p110/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p110/r5.claim: At a stop on al-fajr, tafkhim is the more appropriate treatment of raa.

NASHR:v2p91/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p91/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p91/r1.claim: These rules concern raa not treated in the imala chapter: readings with imala or an intermediate sound make those raa light, while readings with full fatḥ make them emphatic.
NASHR:v2p91/r1.anchor: واعلم أن هذا التقسيم إنما يرد على الراءات التي لم يجر لها ذكر في باب الإمالة

NASHR:v2p91/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p91/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p91/r2.claim: He classifies raa as moving or quiescent; moving raa may be open, rounded, or kasra-bearing, and the open form is catalogued by word position and the preceding vowel or sukun.
NASHR:v2p91/r2.anchor: (فاعلم) أن الراء لا تخلو من أن تكون متحركة أو ساكنة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r1.claim: Alusi cites a report in which the Prophet says God ordered him to recite to someone, then gives a recitation with wording on the true religion and the disputes of the People of the Book.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r1.anchor: قال لي رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r2.claim: Alusi gives al-Ḥākim’s version adding the saying that a person who receives one valley of wealth will ask for another, and only earth fills Adam’s belly; God accepts repentance.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r2.anchor: وفي رواية الحاكم فقرأ فيها ولو أن ابن آدم سأل واديا من مال فأعطيه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r3.claim: The passage also reports that someone wrote the two additional suras called al-Khalaʿ and al-Ḥafd in his codex, classifying this with similar reports.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r3.anchor: وما روى عنه أيضا أنه كتب في مصحفه سورتي الخلع والحفد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r4.speaker: ابن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r4.claim: Through Abū ʿUbayd, Alusi cites Ibn ʿUmar warning people not to claim they have the whole Qur’an, since much had gone, but to say they have what appeared of it; Alusi interprets such reports within his preceding discussion.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r4.anchor: ما رواه أبو عبيد عن ابن عمر قال لا يقولن أحدكم قد أخذت القرآن كله وما يدريه ما كله

ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r5.claim: Alusi rejects the polemical claim that the Qur’an’s present form proves it was already collected as one complete codex in the Prophet’s lifetime; the cited evidence does not establish that.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r5.anchor: ومن لم يجعل الله له نورا فماله من نور

ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r6.claim: He accepts that the Qur’an’s verses and suras were ordered as now and recited from memory in the Prophet’s time while written on separate materials; he rejects the claim that it was then one bound codex.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r6.anchor: إن القرآن كان على عهد رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم مجموعا مؤلفا على ما هو عليه الآن

ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r7.claim: Alusi says the standard codex has 114 suras by accepted consensus, with a reported count of 113 if al-Anfāl and Barāʾah are counted as one.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r8.claim: Alusi says Ibn Masʿūd’s codex had 112 suras; he omitted the protective suras, reportedly called them prayers, and no Companion followed him. Since he recited them in prayer, Alusi rejects the claim that he only opposed writing them.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r8.anchor: وفي مصحف ابن مسعود مائة وإثنتا عشرة سورة لأنه لم يكتب المعوذتين بل صح عنه أنه كان يحكهما من المصاحف

ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r9.claim: Alusi says Ubayy’s codex had 115 suras, including al-Khalaʿ and al-Ḥafd, and combined al-Fīl with Quraysh as one sura.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r9.anchor: وفي مصحف أبي خمسة عشرة لأنه كتب في آخره

ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r10.claim: Alusi lists divergent codex orders: Ibn Masʿūd placed al-Fajr after al-Taḥrīm; Ubayy placed al-Isrāʾ after al-Kahf, al-Ḥujurāt after Nūn, al-Mulk after al-Ḥujurāt, al-Nāziʿāt after al-Wāqiʿah, and al-Sharḥ after al-Ikhlāṣ.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r10.anchor: وسورة ( بني إسرائيل ) في مصحف أبي بعد ( الكهف )

ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r11.claim: Alusi says attribution of the codex collection to ʿUthmān and his companions is widely established, even among Shiʿis, and attributes denials to sectarian prejudice.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r11.anchor: مع أن نسبة هذا الجمع إليهما من أوضح الأمور بل أشهر من المشهور وهو شائع أيضا عند الشيعة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r12.claim: Alusi concludes that the order of both verses and suras is prophetic; he says verse order is unquestionably fixed and cites a consensus reported by al-Zarkashī and Abū Jaʿfar.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p25/r12.anchor: فأعلم أن ترتيب آية وسوره بتوقيف من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r1.claim: Kitab is originally a generic, unrestricted noun or a known referent; with the latter sense it names the Quran's verses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r1.anchor: أنزل عليك الكتاب منه آيات محكمات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r2.claim: An ayah is a portion of Quranic text, whether complete by explicit wording, understood by ellipsis, or counted by inclusion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r2.anchor: هي مقدار من القرآن مركب ولو تقديرا أو إلحاقا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r3.claim: The implicit construction in mدهامتان supplies a subject, while al-Fajr implies an oath verb, as in I swear by the dawn.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r3.anchor: فقولي ولو تقديرا لإدخال قوله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r4.claim: Some disconnected opening letters are counted as verses in the codices, while Alif Lam Ra, Alif Lam Mim Ra, and Ta Sin are excluded; this is an established, transmitted convention with no evident distinction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r4.anchor: فقد عد أكثرها في المصاحف آيات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r5.claim: Calling Quranic portions ayat is a Quranic innovation, as shown in its descriptions of the book's verses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r5.anchor: هذه الأجزاء آيات هو من مبتكرات القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r6.claim: An ayah is a sign of revelation because its composition reaches the highest eloquence; verses together also prove the Quran is divine, since human eloquent speakers failed the challenge to match a surah.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r6.anchor: وإنما سميت آية لأنها دليل على أنها موحى بها من عند الله إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لأنها تشتمل على ما هو من الحد الأعلى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r7.claim: Torah and Gospel clauses should not be called ayat, since Hebrew and Aramaic do not share the Quran's distinctive linguistic quality.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r7.anchor: فلذا لا يحق لجمل التوراة والإنجيل أن تسمى آيات إذ ليست فيها هذه الخصوصية في اللغة العبرانية والآرامية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r8.claim: In the report about the stoning of two Jews, the narrator's phrase ayat al-rajm is an analogical expression for a Torah passage, used because he lacked another name for it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r8.anchor: فذلك تعبير غلب على لسان الراوي على وجه المشاكلة التقديرية تشبيها بجمل القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r9.claim: Verse boundaries are transmitted from the Prophet; varying reports about some boundaries reflect latitude in where those verses end and the next begins, and the Companions knew the divisions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r9.anchor: وتحديد مقادير الآيات مروي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقد تختلف الرواية في بعض الآيات وهو محمول على التخيير في حد تلك الآيات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p18/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p18/r1.speaker: إبراهيم بن علقمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p18/r1.claim: Ibrahim ibn ʿAlqama reports from al-Aʿmash that Qur'anic addresses “O believers” are Medinan and “O people” are Meccan.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p18/r1.anchor: عن إبراهيم بن علقمة: كل شيء في القرآن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p18/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p18/r2.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p18/r2.claim: Maymun ibn Mihran gives a related rule: “O people” and “O children of Adam” indicate Meccan, while “O believers” indicates Medinan.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p18/r2.anchor: عن أبي المليح، عن ميمون بن مهران، قال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p18/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p18/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p18/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir notes that some scholars say certain surahs were revealed twice, once in Mecca and once in Medina; others classify particular verses, such as verses in al-Hajj, differently from their surah.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p18/r3.anchor: ومنهم من يقول: إن بعض السور

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p18/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p18/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p18/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir's rule is to follow sound evidence when deciding whether material is Meccan or Medinan.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p18/r4.anchor: والحق في ذلك ما دل عليه الدليل الصحيح، فالله أعلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p18/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p18/r5.speaker: علي بن أبي طلحة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p18/r5.claim: A report from ʿAli ibn Abi Talha lists surahs and passages said to have been revealed in Medina, including al-Fajr, and says the remainder was Meccan; Ibn Kathir calls its chain authentic and notes that the list includes questionable surahs and omits al-Hujurat and the protective surahs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p18/r5.anchor: قال: نزلت بالمدينة سورة البقرة، وآل عمران، والنساء، والمائدة، والأنفال، والتوبة، والحج، والنور

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p18/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p18/r6.speaker: أبو عثمان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p18/r6.claim: Abu ʿUthman reports that Gabriel visited the Prophet while Umm Salama was present, appearing as Dihya al-Kalbi; she recognized the truth when the Prophet later identified the visitor as Gabriel.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p18/r6.anchor: عن أبي عثمان قال: أنبئت أن جبريل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p18/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p18/r7.speaker: أسامة بن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p18/r7.claim: Abu ʿUthman identifies Usama ibn Zayd as his source for the account; Bukhari and Muslim transmit it through additional routes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p18/r7.anchor: فقلت لأبي عثمان: ممن سمعت هذا؟ فقال: من أسامة بن زيد

BURHAN:v1p72/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p72/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v1p72/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says rhyme should be preserved only when meanings and structure remain sound; sounding ornament alone is not eloquence, and some word order serves exclusivity rather than rhyme.
BURHAN:v1p72/r1.anchor: لا تحسن المحافظة على الفواصل لمجردها إلا مع بقاء المعانى على سدادها على النهج الذى يقتضيه حسن النظم

BURHAN:v1p72/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p72/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p72/r2.claim: Fawasil may have identical or merely close final letters; either is praiseworthy when natural and meaning-led, while forced endings that distort meaning are blameworthy. The Qur'an uses the natural forms.
BURHAN:v1p72/r2.anchor: فالقسم الأول هو المحمود الدال على الثقافة وحسن البيان والثانى هو المذموم

BURHAN:v1p72/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p72/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p72/r3.claim: The yāʾ is dropped from يسر to match the sūra's verse endings.
BURHAN:v1p72/r3.anchor: وحذفت الياء من ﴿ يسر ﴾ طلبا للموافقة فى الفواصل

BURHAN:v1p100/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p100/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p100/r8.claim: The one-word openings of al-Tur, al-Rahman, al-Haqqa, al-Qari'a, and al-Asr are counted by analogy with al-Fajr and al-Duha for rhyme, though their quantities differ.
BURHAN:v1p100/r8.anchor: ﴿ والطور ﴾ و ﴿ الرحمن ﴾ و ﴿ الحاقة ﴾ و ﴿ القارعة ﴾ و ﴿ والعصر ﴾ حملا على

BURHAN:v1p179#2/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p179#2/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p179#2/r1.claim: Fifteen sūras open with an oath, including al-Fajr and al-Asr; this is the fifth listed mode of sūra opening.
BURHAN:v1p179#2/r1.anchor: الخامس القسم نحو ﴿ والصافات ﴾ ﴿ والذاريات ﴾ ﴿ والطور ﴾ ﴿ والنجم ﴾

BURHAN:v1p193/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p193/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p193/r1.claim: In the reported Meccan revelation order, al-Fajr comes ninth, after al-Layl and before al-Duha.
BURHAN:v1p193/r1.anchor: ثم ﴿ والليل إذا يغشى ﴾ ثم ﴿ والفجر ﴾ ثم ﴿ والضحى ﴾

BURHAN:v1p251/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p251/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p251/r4.claim: Verse-count differences arise because the Prophet paused at verse endings by instruction, but sometimes continued to complete the sense, leading listeners to think a boundary was absent.
BURHAN:v1p251/r4.anchor: واعلم أن سبب اختلاف العلماء فى عد الآى والكلم والحروف أن النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقف على رءوس الآى للتوقيف

BURHAN:v1p251/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p251/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p251/r6.claim: Word-count disagreements reflect the fact that a word can be assessed by its literal or figurative meaning, its written form, or convention; scholars choose among these valid measures.
BURHAN:v1p251/r6.anchor: وسبب الاختلاف فى الكلمة أن الكلمة لها حقيقة ومجاز ورسم واعتبار كل منها جائز

BURHAN:v1p251/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p251/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p251/r8.claim: The debt verse is longest at 128 words and 540 letters; al-Duha then al-Fajr are shortest. He rejects مدهامتان and ثم نظر as shorter candidates based on their letter or word counts.
BURHAN:v1p251/r8.anchor: وأطول آية فيه آية الدين مائة وثمانية وعشرون كلمة وخمسمائة وأربعون حرفا

BURHAN:v1p251/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p251/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p251/r10.claim: The shortest word includes the preposition ب, one letter rather than two, contrary to al-Dani's view.
BURHAN:v1p251/r10.anchor: وأقصرها نحو باء الجر حرف واحد لا أنها حرفان خلافا للدانى

BURHAN:v1p267/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p267/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v1p267/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says verse boundaries are fixed by revelation, not analogy; Kufans count some fawātiḥ as verses, while other schools count none of them.
BURHAN:v1p267/r1.anchor: وقال الزمخشرى الآيات علم توقيف لا مجال للقياس فيه

BURHAN:v1p267/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p267/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p267/r4.claim: A word is a single utterance, potentially two to ten letters; al-Fajr, al-Duha, and al-Asr can each be a one-word verse, as can some opening letters for Kufans.
BURHAN:v1p267/r4.anchor: وأما الكلمة فهى اللفظة الواحدة وقد تكون على حرفين مثل ما ولى وله ولك

ITQAN:v1p37/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p37/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p37/r1.claim: Al-Suyuti describes the preceding report as transmitted in full with a good chain whose narrators are reliable, renowned Arab scholars.
ITQAN:v1p37/r1.anchor: هكذا أخرجه بطوله وإسناده جيد رجاله كلهم ثقات من علماء العربية المشهورين

ITQAN:v1p37/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p37/r2.speaker: عكرمة والحسن بن أبي الحسن
ITQAN:v1p37/r2.claim: Al-Bayhaqi transmits from Ikrima and al-Hasan that al-Fajr and al-Asr are among the surahs revealed in Mecca; he also lists surahs revealed in Medina.
ITQAN:v1p37/r2.anchor: وقال البيهقي في دلائل النبوة أنبأنا أبو عبد الله الحافظ أخبرنا أبو محمد بن زياد العدل

ITQAN:v1p38/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p38/r1.speaker: البيهقي
ITQAN:v1p38/r1.claim: Al-Bayhaqi explains that “the ninth” in the preceding report means Yunus, and says al-Fatiha, al-A'raf, and Maryam were omitted from its Meccan list.
ITQAN:v1p38/r1.anchor: قال البيهقي والتاسعة يريد بها سورة يونس قال وقد سقط من هذه الرواية الفاتحة والأعراف وكهيعص فيما نزل بمكة

ITQAN:v1p38/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p38/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v1p38/r2.claim: A report through Mujahid from Ibn Abbas names “Read in the name of your Lord” as the first revelation and supplies a witness to the earlier Meccan-surah report.
ITQAN:v1p38/r2.anchor: حدثنا خصيف عن مجاهد عن ابن عباس أنه قال إن أول ما أنزل الله على نبيه من القرآن ﴿ اقرأ باسم ربك ﴾

ITQAN:v1p38/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p38/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v1p38/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says a surah's opening, when revealed in Mecca, was written there and God could later add to it; his chronology places al-Fajr after al-Layl and before al-Duha.
ITQAN:v1p38/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال كانت إذا أنزلت فاتحة سورة بمكة كتبت بمكة ثم يزيد الله فيها ما شاء

ITQAN:v1p39/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p39/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طلحة
ITQAN:v1p39/r1.claim: Ali ibn Abi Talha's transmitted Medinan list includes al-Fajr, along with al-Layl and other sūras.
ITQAN:v1p39/r1.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طلحة قال نزلت بالمدينة سورة البقرة وآل عمران

ITQAN:v1p39/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p39/r2.speaker: قتادة
ITQAN:v1p39/r2.claim: Qatada's Medinan list omits al-Fajr and says the rest of the Qur'an was revealed in Mecca, implying al-Fajr is Meccan in this account.
ITQAN:v1p39/r2.anchor: عن قتادة قال نزل في المدينة من القرآن البقرة وآل عمران والنساء

ITQAN:v1p39/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p39/r3.speaker: ابن الحصار
ITQAN:v1p39/r3.claim: Ibn al-Hassar classifies twenty sūras as Medinan by agreement, twelve as disputed, and all remaining sūras as Meccan by agreement.
ITQAN:v1p39/r3.anchor: المدني باتفاق عشرون سورة والمختلف فيه اثنتا عشرة سورة وما عدا ذلك مكي باتفاق

ITQAN:v1p77#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p77#2/r1.speaker: علي بن الحسين
ITQAN:v1p77#2/r1.claim: Ali ibn al-Husayn says Iqra was the first Meccan revelation, with al-Muʾminun or al-ʿAnkabut last; al-Mutaffifin began the Medinan revelations, Baraʾa ended them, and al-Najm was the first sūra publicly recited at Mecca.
ITQAN:v1p77#2/r1.anchor: قال سمعت علي بن الحسين يقول أول سورة نزلت بمكة ﴿ اقرأ باسم ربك ﴾ وآخر سورة نزلت بها المؤمنون

ITQAN:v1p77#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p77#2/r2.speaker: ابن حجر
ITQAN:v1p77#2/r2.claim: Ibn Hajar reports agreement that al-Baqara was the first sūra revealed in Medina.
ITQAN:v1p77#2/r2.anchor: وفي شرح البخاري لابن حجر اتفقوا على أن سورة البقرة أول سورة أنزلت بالمدينة

ITQAN:v1p77#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p77#2/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p77#2/r3.claim: Al-Suyuti questions the claimed agreement about al-Baqara because of the preceding report from Ali ibn al-Husayn.
ITQAN:v1p77#2/r3.anchor: وفي دعوى الاتفاق نظر لقول علي بن الحسين المذكور

ITQAN:v1p77#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p77#2/r4.speaker: الواقدي
ITQAN:v1p77#2/r4.claim: Al-Waqidi is cited for the view that al-Qadr was the first sūra revealed in Medina.
ITQAN:v1p77#2/r4.anchor: عن الواقدي إن أول سورة نزلت بالمدينة سورة القدر

ITQAN:v1p77#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p77#2/r5.speaker: جابر بن زيد
ITQAN:v1p77#2/r5.claim: Jabir ibn Zayd's reported Meccan revelation order places al-Fajr tenth and al-ʿAsr thirteenth.
ITQAN:v1p77#2/r5.anchor: عن جابر بن زيد قال أول ما أنزل الله من القرآن بمكة

ITQAN:v1p176/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p176/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
ITQAN:v1p176/r1.claim: The reported order of Ibn Masʿud's codex places al-Fajr and al-ʿAsr among the mufassal sūras, with al-Fajr preceding al-ʿAsr.
ITQAN:v1p176/r1.anchor: تأليف مصحف عبد الله بن مسعود الطوال البقرة والنساء وآل عمران

ITQAN:v1p188/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p188/r1.speaker: الموصلي
ITQAN:v1p188/r1.claim: Al-Mawsili says “then he looked” is the Qur'an's shortest verse; ʿAmma, al-Fajr, and al-Duha are equally short.
ITQAN:v1p188/r1.anchor: قال الموصلي وعدوا قوله ﴿ ثم نظر ﴾ آية وليس في القرآن أقصر منها أما مثلها فعم والفجر والضحى

ITQAN:v3p57/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p57/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ITQAN:v3p57/r1.claim: One classification puts al-Fajr among sūras containing neither abrogating nor abrogated material, while placing al-ʿAsr among sūras containing both.
ITQAN:v3p57/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم سور القرآن باعتبار الناسخ والمنسوخ أقسام قسم ليس فيه ناسخ ولا منسوخ

ITQAN:v3p57/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p57/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p57/r2.claim: Al-Suyuti says this four-part classification of sūras according to abrogation is open to question, as later discussion shows.
ITQAN:v3p57/r2.anchor: كذا قال وفيه نظر يعرف مما سيأتي

ITQAN:v3p57/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p57/r3.speaker: مكي
ITQAN:v3p57/r3.claim: Makki distinguishes an obligation abrogated by another obligation when the former can no longer be practiced, exemplified by confinement of adulteresses replaced by the penalty.
ITQAN:v3p57/r3.anchor: قال مكي الناسخ أقسام فرض نسخ فرضا ولا يجوز العمل بالأول

ITQAN:v3p57/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p57/r4.speaker: مكي
ITQAN:v3p57/r4.claim: Makki also identifies an obligation replaced by another obligation while the earlier obligation may still be practiced, as with the verse of steadfastness.
ITQAN:v3p57/r4.anchor: وفرض نسخ فرضا ويجوز العمل بالأول كآية المصابرة

ITQAN:v3p57/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p57/r5.speaker: مكي
ITQAN:v3p57/r5.claim: Makki's third case is a recommended act later made obligatory, such as fighting first being recommended and then required.
ITQAN:v3p57/r5.anchor: وفرض نسخ ندبا كالقتال كان ندبا ثم صار فرضا

ITQAN:v3p57/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p57/r6.speaker: مكي
ITQAN:v3p57/r6.claim: Makki's fourth case is a recommended act replacing an obligation: night vigil was replaced by reciting what is easy of the Qur'an.
ITQAN:v3p57/r6.anchor: وندب نسخ فرضا كقيام الليل نسخ بالقراءة في قوله ﴿ فاقرؤوا ما تيسر من القرآن ﴾

ITQAN:v3p57/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p57/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p57/r7.claim: Al-Suyuti divides Qur'anic abrogation into three kinds and begins with cases where both the recitation and ruling are abrogated.
ITQAN:v3p57/r7.anchor: النسخ في القرآن على ثلاثة أضرب أحدها ما نسخ تلاوته وحكمه معا

ITQAN:v3p57/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p57/r8.speaker: عائشة
ITQAN:v3p57/r8.claim: Aisha reports that ten known instances of nursing were revealed, then replaced by five; she said the wording was still being recited at the Prophet's death, and the report is in both Ṣaḥīḥs.
ITQAN:v3p57/r8.anchor: قالت عائشة كان فيما أنزل ( عشر رضعات معلومات فنسخن بخمس معلومات فتوفي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهن مما يقرأ من القرآن )

ITQAN:v3p57/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p57/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p57/r9.claim: Al-Suyuti notes the apparent implication that the nursing wording remained recited and explains that its recitation was either abrogated near the Prophet's death or not known to everyone until after his death.
ITQAN:v3p57/r9.anchor: وقد تكلموا في قولها ( وهن مما يقرأ ) فإن ظاهره بقاء التلاوة وليس كذلك

ITQAN:v3p57/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p57/r10.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
ITQAN:v3p57/r10.claim: Abu Musa al-Ashʿari says the nursing passage was revealed and then withdrawn.
ITQAN:v3p57/r10.anchor: وقال أبو موسى الأشعري نزلت ثم رفعت

ITQAN:v3p57/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p57/r11.speaker: مكي
ITQAN:v3p57/r11.claim: Makki says the nursing example is unusual because neither the abrogated text nor its abrogator is recited, and he knows no parallel.
ITQAN:v3p57/r11.anchor: وقال مكي هذا المثال فيه المنسوخ غير متلو والناسخ أيضا غير متلو ولا أعلم له نظيرا

ITQAN:v3p57/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p57/r12.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p57/r12.claim: The second kind removes a ruling while leaving its recitation; despite extensive lists, this kind is truly rare, as Ibn al-ʿArabi carefully showed.
ITQAN:v3p57/r12.anchor: الضرب الثاني ما نسخ حكمه دون تلاوته وهذا الضرب هو الذي فيه الكتب المؤلفة

ITQAN:v3p282/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p282/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p282/r1.claim: Al-Suyuti says all sūras begin in one of ten forms of speech; the oath is the fifth form and opens fifteen sūras.
ITQAN:v3p282/r1.anchor: افتتح سور القرآن بعشرة أنواع من الكلام لا يخرج شيء من السور عنها

ITQAN:v3p282/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p282/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p282/r2.claim: The oath by al-Fajr refers to the beginning of the day.
ITQAN:v3p282/r2.anchor: الفجر بمبدأ النهار والشمس بآية النهار

ITQAN:v4p353/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p353/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p353/r6.claim: The answer to an oath is often omitted when the object sworn by already indicates the assertion; that omission is more forceful and concise.
ITQAN:v4p353/r6.anchor: وأكثر ما يحذف الجواب إذا كان في نفس المقسم به دلالة على المقسم عليه

ITQAN:v4p353/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p353/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p353/r7.claim: The Fajr passage invokes times containing the great rites of pilgrimage and humble worship of God; their significance implies the honor of what Muhammad and Abraham brought.
ITQAN:v4p353/r7.anchor: والفجر ﴾ الآيات فإنها أزمان تتضمن أفعالا معظمة من المناسك وشعائر الحج

ITQAN:v4p431/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p431/r7.speaker: بعضهم
ITQAN:v4p431/r7.claim: An unnamed authority calls al-Baqara the longest sūra, al-Kawthar the shortest, the debt verse the longest āya, al-Duha and al-Fajr the shortest, and “fa-asqaynākumūhu” the longest written word.
ITQAN:v4p431/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم أطول سورة في القرآن البقرة وأقصرها الكوثر وأطول آية فيه آية الدين

ITQAN:v4p447#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p447#2/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p447#2/r3.claim: The source catalogs added alifs after waw in plural nouns and in certain verb forms, with listed exceptions.
ITQAN:v4p447#2/r3.anchor: زيدت ألف بعد الواو آخر اسم مجموع نحو ( بنوا إسرائيل ) ( ملاقوا ربهم )

ITQAN:v4p447#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p447#2/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p447#2/r4.claim: It also lists added alifs after hamza written as waw and in several specific forms, including “miʾa,” “miʾatayn,” and definite nouns ending in alif.
ITQAN:v4p447#2/r4.anchor: وبعد الهمزة المرسومة واوا نحو ( تفتؤا ) وفي مائة ومائتين والظنونا

ITQAN:v4p447#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p447#2/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p447#2/r5.claim: The orthography adds yāʾ in several listed forms, including “nabāʾ al-mursalīn,” “malāʾihi,” and “bi-ayydikum.”
ITQAN:v4p447#2/r5.anchor: وزيدت ياء في ( نبائ المرسلين ) و ( ملإيه ) ( ملإيهم )

ITQAN:v4p447#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p447#2/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p447#2/r6.claim: An extra wāw is written in “ulū” and its derivatives, and in “sa-urīkum.”
ITQAN:v4p447#2/r6.anchor: وزيدت واو في ( أولوا ) وفروعه و ( سأوريكم )

ITQAN:v4p447#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p447#2/r7.speaker: الكرماني
ITQAN:v4p447#2/r7.claim: Al-Kirmani explains some extra letters as remnants of an older script in which alif, wāw, and yāʾ represented the short vowels fatḥa, ḍamma, and kasra.
ITQAN:v4p447#2/r7.anchor: وقال الكرماني في العجائب كانت صورة الفتحة في الخطوط قبل الخط العربي ألفا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p192/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p192/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p192/r1.claim: A poet heightens ink's blackness by likening it to night; Jurjani suggests al-Buḥturī adapted the common saying that something black is like ink, then changed it for rhyme.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p192/r1.anchor: وكأن البحترى نظر إلى قول العامة في الشىء الأسود هو كالنقس ثم تركه للقافية

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p192/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p192/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p192/r2.claim: Jurjani answers that dawn can resemble a horse's blaze despite their difference in brightness, because the intended likeness is a small white patch appearing against darkness, not equal luminosity.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p192/r2.anchor: فإن تشبيه غرة الفرس بالصبح حيث ذكرت لم يقع من جهة المبالغة في وصفها بالضياء والانبساط

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p192/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p192/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p192/r3.claim: The comparison works in reverse too: first dawn in the night can appear as a blaze on a dark horse, just as a white mark shows on black silk.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p192/r3.anchor: كان الصبح عند ظهور أوله في الليل غرة في فرس أدهم

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p192/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p192/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p192/r4.claim: Ibn al-Muʿtazz's brocade image makes dawn the white mark on a dark, starry garment, confirming that the comparison concerns contrast rather than equal size.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p192/r4.anchor: العلم في هذا الرداء هو الفجر بلا شبهة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p192/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p192/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p192/r5.claim: Another poem makes dawn a decorative trim on night, a sound comparison despite the disparity in their extent because it rests on a bright band set against darkness.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p192/r5.anchor: وإن كان التفاوت في المقدار بين الصبح والطراز في الامتداد والانبساط شديدا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p192/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p192/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p192/r6.claim: Ibn al-Muʿtazz compares the sun to a polished mirror and a newly minted coin; Jurjani accepts the image because roundness, gleam, and a particular color matter, not comparable size or total light.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p192/r6.anchor: حسن مقبول وإن عظم التفاوت بين نور الشمس ونور المرآة والدينار أو الجرم

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p192/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p192/r7.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p192/r7.claim: The comparison may be reversed: a mirror can be likened to the sun, and scattered coins can be described as little suns.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p192/r7.anchor: ويستقيم لك العكس في هذا كله نحو أن تشبه المرآة بالشمس وكذلك لو قلت في الدينار كأنه شمس

DAMGHANI:v1p350/r9.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p350/r9.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p350/r9.anchor: الفجر الصبح قوله تعالى في سورة الفجر والفجر وليال عشر
